love-test.title: Love Test
love-test.syn:
An empty room, flickering lights, bodies entwined in the dark and a face both strange and familiar. When pianist Ding Boyang’s girlfriend Wan Ying suddenly disappears, he stops sleeping and drinks to forget, soon growing close to a young waitress, Ma Ya, and bringing her home to his secluded villa in the hills.

Once Ma Ya moves in, uncanny things begin to happen, and a key of unknown origin leads her step by step toward the truth of Wan Ying’s disappearance. The vanishing was meant as a test of love, and from the moment Ma Ya stepped into the house she, too, became a player in this dangerous game. Intimacy or estrangement, devotion or cruelty: all three are trapped in a contest of human nature.
love-test.bio:
Born in Beijing in 1987, Hou Xiaoyao graduated from the Central Academy of Drama and started out in editing and assistant directing, serving as assistant director and editor on Hou Keming’s film Heading North (2012). In November 2020, Hengye Pictures announced a remake of the Spanish-language thriller The Hidden Face with Hou directing; it became Love Test, which started shooting in Shanghai in October 2021.

Love Test is his first theatrical feature, executive-produced by Lu Yang (the Brotherhood of Blades films, A Writer’s Odyssey) and veteran producer Wang Hongwei, and co-written with Xu Xiaohu. Another feature he directed, The Long Night (also known as Sea Without Night, starring Geng Le and Qiu Tian), has yet to be released. Discussing the title, he has said that testing in a relationship is mutual suspicion: on the surface two women test one man, but the man is also testing where each of them stands.
love-test.st:
The film adapts Andrés Baiz’s 2011 Spanish-language thriller The Hidden Face (La cara oculta, promoted in China as a Spanish film), which had also been remade in Korea. The Chinese version moves the story to a secluded villa in the hills. It is produced by Zhijiang Film (Zhejiang) and Tianjin Maoyan Weiying, with Beijing Free Whale Pictures, Yunnan Jincai Shijie and others co-producing. The crew includes cinematographer Yu Lik-wai, gaffer Huang Zhiming, production designer Liu Weixin, editor Li Nanyi, costume and make-up designer Wang Tao, sound supervisor Lin Siyu and composer Ding Ke.

Feng Shaofeng plays Ding Boyang, a pianist who is refined on the surface and obsessive underneath; Chen Yusi plays Ma Ya and Li Meng plays Wan Ying, with Guo Yue, Che Xiao, Zhou Yemang and Yang Yi in supporting roles. The director has shared a behind-the-scenes detail: while Feng and Chen shot their scenes together, Li Meng would sit behind the monitor noting how each line was picked up and where each hand went, then later replay those reactions alone. At a Chengdu screening he also explained that the dog barking Ma Ya hears alone in the house and the later scene of a police dog barking at a mirror were cut from the same scene split across time, planted as a clue.

Shooting began on October 25, 2021, with a “playing with fire” poster of three matches. The film then sat on the shelf for years before being presented at the 8th Zhejiang International Youth Film Week’s new-releases showcase in September 2025. Its release date was announced on October 26, 2026, and it opened in Mainland China on November 21, taking about 4.6 million yuan on its first day with roughly 10.6% of screenings. Runtime: 106 minutes.
highlights: The title is the key: watch who is testing whom. The director calls it mutual suspicion, with the male lead testing both women in return.
The hillside villa is a fourth character. Doors, mirrors and a key keep returning; note which details are later reinterpreted.
Much of Li Meng’s role is reaction work in which she can only watch. The director says she studied her co-stars’ scenes from behind the monitor before replaying them alone.
If you have seen The Hidden Face, compare the Chinese version’s localisation and whether its added jump scares change the original’s psychological restraint.
On November 26 there is a roadshow screening at Zheying Shidai Xiguang in Hangzhou, with director Hou Xiaoyao attending a post-screening Q&A.
love-test.editorial: For viewers who like one-house, three-person psychological suspense and stories about control and suspicion in relationships. It adapts the well-regarded The Hidden Face, and its structure and twists are intact, but reception has been poor (4.8 on Douban): many viewers feel the remake leans too heavily on jump-scare sound effects and doesn’t dig deep enough into motives. Fans of the original may miss its restraint; newcomers who just want a twisty thriller may have an easier time. There is a director Q&A roadshow screening in Hangzhou on November 26.
love-test.contentNote: Checked against the official synopsis, promotional materials and public post-release reviews: the story centres on a partner’s disappearance and on manipulation and deception in the name of love, with a horror-thriller atmosphere, sudden jump-scare images and sound, and sexual innuendo and intimate scenes. No official rating notes or scene-by-scene review have been obtained; explicitness and sensory items such as flashing lights remain unverified. These topic notes are not an official rating.

screeningNotes.11/26-19:00-hz-zy-xiguang-hall-1: Post-screening event · Director: Hou Xiaoyao · Post-screening Q&A 20:50–21:10 (subject to who actually attends) · Free admission

py26-break.title: Break
py26-break.syn: Dong Jie returns to film his former middle-school politics teacher Sheng Liming over the National Day holiday. The assignment changes direction when they hear that Li Yanwu, one of Dong’s former classmates, has disappeared. Sheng grows increasingly invested in the search, and Dong begins to reconsider what keeping the camera running means.
honors: Screened | 2019 Beijing Film Academy graduation showcase
Screened | 2019 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao Corner
Screened | Beijing International Short Film Festival
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-break.contentNote: The published synopsis touches on interpersonal strain. Sound and light intensity await verification.
py26-break.editorial: Notice when Sheng volunteers a memory and when the camera waits for one. The teacher and pupil’s relationship changes with the direction of the filming.
py26-break.bio: Dong Jie studied directing at Beijing Film Academy and also works as a writer and editor. His graduation film Break screened at Pingyao Corner and the Beijing International Short Film Festival. He later explored virtual models and physical streets in Beijing Mushroom and returned to a missing-person story in his feature debut Zoom In, Zoom Out.
py26-break.st: Dong wrote, directed and edited the film, and plays the camera-carrying student under his own name. The assignment provides an in-story reason to film the teacher’s routines and the search. Because the filmmaker within the story also knew the missing student, his decision to keep recording has a personal stake.
highlights: Pair it with Zoom In, Zoom Out to compare a search through the memories of former classmates with a search through a networked game.

py26-ray-of-sunshine.title: The Ray of Sunshine
py26-ray-of-sunshine.syn: A young restaurant cook loses his job after a fight. He accompanies his girlfriend, a server at the same restaurant, to the hospital for a check-up. Employment and uncertainty about her health collide over a single day, as both come to understand what the other is facing.
honors: Official Selection | 2019 FIRST International Film Festival · Short Competition
Screened | 2019 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao Corner
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
warnings: Job loss, medical examination and financial strain
py26-ray-of-sunshine.contentNote: The story involves job loss, a visit for a medical check-up and the couple’s financial strain.
py26-ray-of-sunshine.editorial: Compare the restaurant with the hospital: one can take away a livelihood, the other forces the couple to stop and wait. Both spaces keep pushing the film’s promised tomorrow away.
py26-ray-of-sunshine.bio: Beijing-born Geng Zihan graduated from the Central Academy of Drama. The Ray of Sunshine played in FIRST’s short-film competition and Green Screen later screened at LA Shorts. Her debut feature A Song Sung Blue premiered in Directors’ Fortnight and earned her Pingyao’s Fei Mu directing award.
py26-ray-of-sunshine.st: Geng also produced and edited this short. Hao Jiayue, who returned for A Song Sung Blue, shot it. Lin Yuhan handled production design and Sun Mingjun sound effects. In her FIRST statement Geng focused on how the lovers get through a day of uncertainty. FIRST dates production to 2018 and lists its 2019 screenings as non-premiere engagements.
highlights: Paired with A Song Sung Blue, the short reveals Geng’s interest in people whose needs and feelings are out of step, and in their willingness to wait for each other.

py26-a-song-sung-blue.title: A Song Sung Blue
py26-a-song-sung-blue.syn: When her mother leaves to work abroad, fifteen-year-old Liu Xian moves in with her estranged father, who runs a struggling photo studio. She meets Jin Mingmei, the eighteen-year-old daughter of his assistant. Mingmei gives Liu Xian a reason to venture out, but the two girls have different ideas of what closeness and the future might hold.
honors: World Premiere | 2023 Cannes Directors’ Fortnight
Award | 2023 Pingyao International Film Festival · Fei Mu Award for Best Director
Screened | 2024 Mulan International Film Festival
Screened | 2024 ONE International Women’s Film Festival special screening
Release | Mainland China · 4 July 2025
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-a-song-sung-blue.contentNote: The published synopsis touches on family conflict and adolescent loneliness. Sound and light intensity await verification.
py26-a-song-sung-blue.editorial: Notice what the image and soundtrack reveal when Liu Xian watches Mingmei. The more closely she looks, the easier it is for her to project a possible future onto Mingmei.
py26-a-song-sung-blue.bio: Born in Beijing, Geng studied directing at the Central Academy of Drama. She made The Ray of Sunshine and Green Screen before taking her feature debut to Directors’ Fortnight. The performances of Zhou Meijun and Huang Ziqi anchor the film. Geng won Best Director at Pingyao for the feature.
py26-a-song-sung-blue.st: Liu Yining’s undergraduate feature script became the project, which took shape through a development market with producers Liang Jing and Jane Zheng. In post-screening discussions Geng described staying close to Liu Xian’s experience. Cinematographer Hao Jiayue and the sound department helped shape that subjectivity. Huang and Geng had already collaborated as students.
highlights: The photo studio is worth watching as a space: it produces neatly arranged memories for strangers while housing the untidiest relationships in Liu Xian’s family.

py26-goodbye-mr-kong.title: Goodbye, Mr. Kong
py26-goodbye-mr-kong.syn: Mr Kong has taught at an elementary school in Qufu, Shandong, for thirty years. With his son now starting a family in Beijing, he takes early retirement to care for his grandchild. The film spends his last day at school with him, as familiar places, people and small routines take on the weight of a final visit.
honors: Official Selection | 2017 Nine-Minute Film Championship
Screened | 2017 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao Corner
Screened | 2023 China Film Archive · Kong Dashan shorts programme
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-goodbye-mr-kong.contentNote: The published synopsis touches on farewells and relationships. Sound and light intensity await verification.
py26-goodbye-mr-kong.editorial: Watch the small things that still happen on schedule. The institution keeps running while the teacher’s place within it changes.
py26-goodbye-mr-kong.bio: Kong Dashan graduated from the directing department of Beijing Film Academy. His early shorts include The Long Night and his mock news report on a young cinephile. Goodbye, Mr. Kong takes him back to Qufu for a schoolteacher’s last day. He later directed his debut feature Journey to the West, co-written with Wang Yitong.
py26-goodbye-mr-kong.st: Made for the seventh Nine-Minute Film Championship, the short was written and directed by Kong, produced by Kong Xiaoxia and shot by Sun Xiaochen, with sound by Qiao Mingzi and colour by Liu Pai. Kong Fangang plays a man leaving a professional role and taking on an unpaid role within his family.
highlights: Compare it with Journey to the West: both begin a trip after years of familiar routines, but the pivotal journey here may be the walk Mr Kong has already taken countless times.

py26-journey-to-the-west.title: Journey to the West
py26-journey-to-the-west.syn: Tang Zhijun’s science-fiction magazine is failing, but he is still looking for extraterrestrial life. A report from a village in southwestern China sends him and a small crew on the road, where they meet Sun Yitong, a young man who wears a pot and speaks like a poet. As improbable clues accumulate, the search brings a private grief into view.
honors: World Premiere | 2021 Pingyao International Film Festival · Crouching Tigers
Award | 2021 Pingyao International Film Festival · Fei Mu Award for Best Film
Award | 2023 Golden Rooster Awards · Best Screenplay
Release | Mainland China · 1 April 2023
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-journey-to-the-west.contentNote: The published synopsis touches on bereavement and psychological distress. Sound and light intensity await verification.
py26-journey-to-the-west.editorial: Note the moments when the camera hesitates, fails to keep up or loses focus. The viewer can often establish even less than Tang believes he knows.
py26-journey-to-the-west.bio: Kong graduated from Beijing Film Academy and experimented with fictional television reportage in his short films. His feature debut carried that interest into a road movie and won Best Film in Pingyao’s Fei Mu awards. Kong and co-writer Wang Yitong later won the Golden Rooster screenplay award.
py26-journey-to-the-west.st: Kong and Wang Yitong co-wrote the film. Yang Haoyu plays Tang and Wang plays Sun. The cinematographer is Matthias Delvaux. Kong told The Paper after Pingyao that the team dispensed with conventional slates, lighting and shot breakdowns. The apparent spontaneity comes from a practical shooting method and the room it leaves for performance.
highlights: Listen to Sun’s poetry alongside Tang’s delight in evidence. Each uses an earnest language to approach things that cannot be proved.

py26-mother-eden.title: Mother Eden
py26-mother-eden.syn: Teacher Yao hears that two colleagues at her school have left town after an affair. The news sends her back to her own youth as an idealistic student in the 1980s. Now middle-aged, she reassesses the ambitions and compromises of the life she has built in a small city.
honors: World Premiere | 2018 FIRST International Film Festival · Short Competition
Nomination | 2018 FIRST International Film Festival · Best Short Film
Award | 2018 South Taiwan Film Festival · Best Fiction Short
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-mother-eden.contentNote: The story involves an affair and the departures of two colleagues, as well as memories of work and family.
py26-mother-eden.editorial: Start with the two absent colleagues. Yao’s interpretation of their departure offers a way to hear how she imagines an alternative to her own life.
py26-mother-eden.bio: Hunan-born Wang Erzhuo earned a master’s degree at the Central Academy of Drama. An early documentary screened at Yamagata, and Mother Eden won Best Fiction Short at South Taiwan Film Festival. His first feature went on to win a New Currents award at Busan. Both dramas approach generational change through women’s memories.
py26-mother-eden.st:
Wang traced the film to accounts by his mother and her generation in his FIRST director’s statement. He wrote, directed and edited it, with cinematography by Li Linhan, production design by Yun Dan and sound effects by Wang Xueying. FIRST’s nomination notes drew attention to the way the narration and images lend ordinary life a longer historical reach.

FIRST lists production in 2017 and the premiere in 2018. South Taiwan Film Festival catalogues the film under 2018.
highlights: Notice when the narration takes an image back in time and when it leaves a gap. An individual life here becomes part of a three-generation structure in Farewell, My Hometown.

py26-farewell-my-hometown.title: Farewell, My Hometown
py26-farewell-my-hometown.syn: An older woman in the mountains recalls poverty, labour and the loss of a child. A young woman in the city thinks back to the solitude of dance school in Beijing. A middle-aged teacher takes to the stage and remembers her college years in the 1980s and an earlier love. Mountains, apartments and a stage hold three accounts of leaving and belonging.
honors: World Premiere | 2021 Busan International Film Festival · New Currents
Award | 2021 Busan International Film Festival · New Currents Award
Award | 2021 Pingyao International Film Festival · Fei Mu Special Mention
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
warnings: Death of a child, poverty and personal strain
py26-farewell-my-hometown.contentNote: The accounts involve poverty, hard labour, the death of a child and loneliness after moving away.
py26-farewell-my-hometown.editorial: Listen to each episode as a kind of move. What changes the way a person speaks of home may be less the distance travelled than the rooms she has lived in since.
py26-farewell-my-hometown.bio: Wang Erzhuo grew up in Hunan and received a master’s degree from the Central Academy of Drama. The small-town teacher in Mother Eden gave him a starting point for looking at an older generation. In his debut feature he set three generations alongside one another, winning a New Currents award at Busan.
py26-farewell-my-hometown.st: Wang has said in interview that some of the memories that moved him most were told by women. Busan describes three episodes, placing recollection against mountain scenery, urban apartments and a stage. Spoken memories and visible spaces do not always line up. Busan records an 83-minute world-premiere cut, while this Pingyao listing records 90 minutes.
highlights: After Mother Eden, return to the teacher’s episode. An inward recollection in the short becomes one voice in the feature’s conversation across three generations.

py26-on-the-border.title: On the Border
py26-on-the-border.syn: Hua Dongxing, a Korean-Chinese teenager in the China–North Korea border region, hopes to get to South Korea. He travels from his village to town to ask his father for money, only to find him absent. The planned departure gives way to time spent in a half-familiar border town and the question of whom he can turn to.
honors: Official Selection | 2018 Festival de Cannes · Short Film Competition
Award | 2018 Festival de Cannes · Short Film Jury Special Distinction
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-on-the-border.contentNote: The published synopsis touches on adolescent distress. Sound and light intensity await verification.
py26-on-the-border.editorial: Notice which places allow Hua to linger and which he can only pass through. The border is both his everyday setting and a direction in which he dreams of leaving.
py26-on-the-border.bio: Wei Shujun worked as an actor and studied sound direction at Communication University of China. Duck Neck screened at Busan, and On the Border received a Cannes short-film jury distinction. His later features include Striding into the Wind, Ripples of Life and Only the River Flows.
py26-on-the-border.st: In Cannes-era interviews Wei traced the idea to a trip through Yanji, where he noticed how many young people left for work while older residents stayed behind. Li Zhenming and Cui Yuna star, with cinematography by Wang Jiehong and editing by Chen Shikong. The wider movement of people comes into view through one search for a father.
highlights: Pair it with Only the River Flows: the teenager searches for someone who might fund the journey, while a detective searches for evidence. Neither finds a ready explanation in the people he encounters.

py26-only-the-river-flows.title: Only the River Flows
py26-only-the-river-flows.syn: In a southern Chinese town in the 1990s, a body is found by the river. Detective Ma Zhe sets up in a disused cinema and follows leads into the private lives and rumours of the town. While colleagues want the case closed, each new piece of information unsettles an explanation that had seemed secure.
honors: World Premiere | 2023 Festival de Cannes · Un Certain Regard
Release | Mainland China · 21 October 2023
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
py26-only-the-river-flows.contentNote: The published synopsis touches on murder investigation and violent themes. Sound and light intensity await verification.
py26-only-the-river-flows.editorial: Watch the disused cinema. The detectives arrange leads there almost as if editing the town into a coherent movie. Notice when Ma starts filling in the gaps himself.
py26-only-the-river-flows.bio: Wei studied sound direction at Communication University of China and began in performance. After the Cannes distinction for On the Border, Striding into the Wind was named in the Cannes Official Selection and Ripples of Life played Directors’ Fortnight. Only the River Flows brought his attention to small-town life into a crime narrative and premiered in Un Certain Regard.
py26-only-the-river-flows.st: Wei and Kang Chunlei adapted Yu Hua’s story. Wei has said that the script went through several major versions from 2020, and that he and cinematographer Chengma chose 16mm at the script stage. The team shot in story order. The dream sequence grew out of location scouting and gives the detective a space to arrange what he has seen outside the rules of evidence.
highlights: Watch how film grain, night scenes and the water limit what can be seen. Much of the suspense comes from the film taking away things the viewer thought were visible.
py26-only-the-river-flows.book: Mistakes by the River by Yu Hua

py26-lili-alone.title: Lili Alone
py26-lili-alone.syn: Lili, a young mother in a remote part of Sichuan, lives with a husband who gambles. With her father gravely ill, she heads alone for a southern city and considers becoming a surrogate to pay for his care. The city opens one possible source of income and places her choices within rules set by other people.
honors: World Premiere | 2021 Cannes Critics’ Week · Short Film Competition
Award | 2021 Cannes Critics’ Week · Leitz Cine Discovery Prize for Short Film
Screened | Mulan International Film Festival
Screened | 2026 Pingyao International Film Festival · Pingyao 10 Years
warnings: Grave illness in the family, gambling and surrogacy
py26-lili-alone.contentNote: The story involves grave illness, gambling, surrogacy and financial pressure.
py26-lili-alone.editorial: Notice whom Lili can speak to at home and in the city, and which decisions she must carry alone. The film renders financial pressure through movement, waiting and her body.
py26-lili-alone.bio: Zou Jing worked as a writer and made documentaries for Shanghai television before moving into fiction. She wrote and directed Lili Alone, which competed in Cannes Critics’ Week and won the Leitz Cine Discovery Prize. Her debut feature A Girl Unknown returned to Critics’ Week.
py26-lili-alone.st: Wang Yang and Qiu Yang are credited as producers, with Liangzi as cinematographer, Hsu Yen Ching as editor and Xing Jun in production design. A Critics’ Week essay connects Lili’s opening prayer with a later upward glance on a boat at night. The recurring gesture carries her between two circumstances and gives her a life of attention beyond the financial stakes.
highlights: Notice Lili’s gaze at the opening and on the night boat. The film gives her room to look and gives the viewer time without demanding an immediate explanation for her feelings.

bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.title: Bleda y Rosa. A Place, an Image
bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.o: Bleda y Rosa. Un lloc, una imatge
bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.syn: María Bleda and José María Rosa carry measuring tape, stakes, maps and a tripod into a forest. The two photographers return to the same patch of ground, testing where an object belongs until a new image can be made. The film follows the work from the woods to the gallery and gives the eventual photograph a past you can see and hear.
bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.bio: Spanish filmmaker and producer Xavier Crespo developed the project with originator Carles Candela and writer Silvia Blasco. The subjects, María Bleda and José María Rosa, met at art school in Valencia and received Spain's National Photography Prize in 2008. Their series Football Fields, Battlefields and Origin use landscapes to recall events that have left few visible traces.
bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.st: The project grew out of conversations between Crespo and Candela in 2007 while they were filming sites associated with the end of the Spanish Civil War. They eventually followed the creation of Res Communis. Split screen grew out of synchronised dual-camera material that Eloy Enciso retained in his first edit. The team shot additional material with this relationship in mind, and Amadeo Moscardó designed sound for the two images sharing a space.
bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.editorial: Watch this alongside Otium for two answers to what it takes to make a photograph of a place. Hanna works to a platform's specifications. Bleda and Rosa can spend hours rethinking where to stand. The time missing from both types of photograph becomes the subject here.
highlights: Watch how measuring, staking and walking precede the camera's final position.
Listen for the way one view's sounds influence what you notice in the other.
Compare what the finished photo holds with what you remember from the forest.
honors: 入选｜2026 FIDMarseille · Other Gems (non-competitive, world premiere)
入选｜2026 8th Hainan Island International Film Festival · A Possibility (Asian premiere)
bleda-y-rosa-a-place-an-image.contentNote: Public story and programme information reviewed. Detailed depiction and audiovisual intensity await verification.

foreign-travel-2026.title: Foreign Travel
foreign-travel-2026.syn: Over a year in Berlin, Leonie and a small group of friends read Italian writer Anna Maria Ortese. Their conversations move through courtyards and cafés as people look for flats, settle in a new country and prepare for a child. A visit to Ortese's German translator, Sigrid Vagt, gives Leonie another way to think about the stories taking shape around her.
foreign-travel-2026.bio: Ted Fendt is a filmmaker, translator and projectionist from Philadelphia. He funded early films in the Philadelphia and South Jersey area through his projection work in New York. Short Stay and Classical Period both played the Berlinale Forum. He continued to work as a projectionist and translator after moving to Berlin.
foreign-travel-2026.st: Giovanna Giuliani introduced Fendt to Ortese's writing in Paris. Fendt and Leonie Rodrian developed the film scene by scene, with the other performers free to revise their lines. They filmed one or two days each month on a tight supply of 16mm stock. Jenny Lou Ziegel photographed a single Berlin neighbourhood as its seasons changed.
foreign-travel-2026.editorial: Fans of a good post-screening conversation may recognise the pleasure here. Pay attention to how long Fendt lets a conversation breathe, then how easily he passes over the weeks before the next one. Vagt's account of translation offers a way into those choices.
highlights: Follow shifts in light around the same Berlin streets.
Listen to how Sigrid Vagt explains a translation choice.
Watch the everyday news friends bring to each meeting.
honors: 入选｜2026 Berlin International Film Festival · Forum (world premiere)
入选｜2026 FIDMarseille · International Competition
入选｜2026 New York Film Festival
入选｜2026 8th Hainan Island International Film Festival · A Possibility (Asian premiere)
foreign-travel-2026.contentNote: Public story and programme information reviewed. Detailed depiction and audiovisual intensity await verification.

otium-2026.title: Otium
otium-2026.syn: Hanna travels between Mississauga and Toronto, making ends meet through online tutoring and real-estate photography. The luxury apartments she photographs are often vacant. Back at her parents' house, she tries to hold on to time for her own work. Older family footage puts the life she can afford beside the prosperity previous generations could expect.
otium-2026.bio: Toronto-based Canadian filmmaker Christopher Beaulieu made his feature debut with Otium. He worked with Eliza Martin on a student film years before writing the role of Hanna with her in mind. His own years of gig work in Toronto underpin the film's attention to commuting, awkward friendships and the minutes available for art.
otium-2026.st: Beaulieu had done every job he gives Hanna. He conceived the indifferent circular pan before writing the story and expanded a planned short during the pandemic. He rehearsed broadly framed scenes with the actors and shot on 16mm with Liam Guay. Footage shot in his childhood home meets family recordings of the same place and 8mm material from his grandparents.
otium-2026.editorial: Watch how long the film leaves you in a condo after you have understood what it looks like. The Latin title refers to time available for thought or making things. Hanna's paid labour tells you exactly what it costs her to find that time.
highlights: Notice when the camera keeps moving after Hanna leaves the frame.
Compare the digitally crisp real-estate pictures with the film's 16mm grain.
Listen for the repeated musical movement and see how it meets the family footage.

september-afternoon-2026.title: September Afternoon
september-afternoon-2026.syn: A couple heads to the coast with a child after the weather has turned. The wind defeats their attempts at shelter, the tide threatens a small dam, and sand gets into the ice cream. They are determined to make the afternoon live up to their idea of summer. A series of minor frustrations grows into something closer to a cosmic catastrophe.
september-afternoon-2026.bio: Born in Leipzig in 1979, Nicolaas Schmidt works across film, video and conceptual art in Hamburg. Final Stage won a special jury prize at the 2017 Berlinale, and First Time received a Pardi di Domani special mention at Locarno in 2021. September Afternoon is his first feature.
september-afternoon-2026.st: Schmidt wrote, directed and edited the film, photographed by Thomas Oswald. An ice cream commercial from the 1980s opens the film with a promise of effortless fun. On the actual beach, repetitive music and prolonged physical tasks stretch that promise to breaking point. The film goes without spoken dialogue.
september-afternoon-2026.editorial: Keep the advertisement in mind as the film returns to the seaside rituals it sells. An umbrella that will not go up first plays as physical comedy. The length of the struggle gives it room to become something stranger.
highlights: Compare the commercial's beach with the actual beach.
Listen to how repeated music changes the tone.
Notice when the repeated action turns from funny to unnerving.

the-birds-tell-me-all-there-is-to-know.title: The Birds Tell Me All There Is To Know
the-birds-tell-me-all-there-is-to-know.o: The Birds Tell Me All There Is To Know
the-birds-tell-me-all-there-is-to-know.syn: As summer ends in upstate New York, a retired painter with dementia tends the birds in his backyard, repeatedly losing hold of the news of his wife's death. Across town, Sam grieves for her father, cares for her mother and faces the imminent departure of a friend. A birdhouse briefly brings their separate routines into contact.
the-birds-tell-me-all-there-is-to-know.bio: Brooklyn-based Aidan Cronin is a filmmaker, cinematographer and programmer who co-founded the Ithaca Experimental Film Festival. He works with older cameras and lenses. This first feature brings that interest into his writing, photography and editing.
the-birds-tell-me-all-there-is-to-know.st: Cronin wrote, directed, photographed and edited the film and was one of its producers. He shot it on Video8, an analogue consumer format that preceded Hi8. The Spectacle screening notes draw attention to the way birds, frogs and water compete with lawn equipment. The filmmaker and Spectacle list the film at 123 minutes. The Green Mountain premiere schedule lists a 153-minute slot.
the-birds-tell-me-all-there-is-to-know.editorial: Give the two characters time to tend to their own lives before expecting the encounter to do anything for them. Listen for the small sounds that come back as the machines quieten. That is one place the film makes room for grief.
highlights: Listen for the shifts between wildlife and lawn machinery.
Follow the birdhouse as it passes between the two stories.
Notice how Video8 handles the small distances in a backyard.

the-mirage-bingham-bryant-2026.title: The Mirage
the-mirage-bingham-bryant-2026.syn: A young French visitor searches for coastal mirages in San Sebastián. On a boat she meets a Portuguese woman who tells her about two sisters who once lived there. The story enters their walks, encounters and obsessions. A figure in an old image seems to move again, and a pair of binoculars used backwards puts other images just within reach.
the-mirage-bingham-bryant-2026.bio: Bingham Bryant is an American filmmaker and producer based in Lisbon and New York. He co-directed For the Plasma with Kyle Molzan and went on to make shorts including Foreign Powers. His solo feature debut returns to optical devices and conflicting points of view.
the-mirage-bingham-bryant-2026.st: Bryant adapted Edogawa Rampo's 1929 story The Traveller with the Pasted Rag Picture. An early version set the story in New York. Moving to San Sebastián led him to use the city's slopes, lifts and sightlines, and to recast the original brothers as sisters. He rehearsed blocking with the actors before cinematographer Christopher Messina joined with the camera. The production lists both HD and 16mm.
the-mirage-bingham-bryant-2026.editorial: Follow the long shots as if you had taken a wrong turn in a city you barely know. Pay attention to the moments when the camera changes perspective without a cut and to how easily a story someone is telling becomes something you appear to have seen yourself.
highlights: Watch how windows, staircases and reflections form frames inside the shot.
Follow the changes in who can see whom as the characters climb or descend.
Recall who first described an image when it reappears.

wild-strawberries.title: Wild Strawberries
wild-strawberries.syn: Isak Borg (Victor Sjöström), a doctor for fifty years and now nearly eighty, is about to travel back to his old university to receive an honorary degree, accompanied by his daughter-in-law. Along the way he revisits places from his past and remembers. Isak once had a tender first love in his cousin Sara (Bibi Andersson), but his cold and withdrawn nature let his brother step in. Now, sitting on the grass, he recalls the past and sees Sara before him in her white dress. His innate coldness and rationality doomed his marriage; his wife, unable to bear its chill, sought affairs elsewhere. Such a household, together with the inherited coldness, has left his son unwilling to have children and estranged from his own wife. Isak receives his honorary degree, yet remains immersed in heavy self-examination — for an old man near the end of his life, it seems a journey of spiritual redemption.
wild-strawberries.bio: Ingmar Bergman was a Swedish film and theatre director and screenwriter, known for The Seventh Seal, Persona, Cries and Whispers and Fanny and Alexander. He often placed family relationships, questions of faith and the self-scrutiny of his characters in a single story, unfolding inner conflict through faces, dreams and everyday conversation.
wild-strawberries.st: Lead actor Victor Sjöström was himself a major director of the Swedish silent era. By casting this elder as the aging professor, Bergman adds a layer of film history to the on-screen act of looking back. Dreams and reality interweave throughout; watch how the same actor appears across different layers of time.
highlights: A clear road trip keeps being interrupted by dreams, and old feelings seep into the present.
The car conversation between the professor and his daughter-in-law is brief; the coldness hides in ordinary replies.

wild-strawberries.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Death and bereavement; Family conflict or separation. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
wild-strawberries.editorial: For anyone interested in memory, dreams and ageing. Meeting old places on the journey matters more than arriving; you'll get more by noticing the characters' silences.

dogville.title: Dogville
dogville.syn:
A mysterious woman, Grace (Nicole Kidman), stumbles into a closed, conservative American town. Beautiful and kind, she is fleeing gangsters. Tom, the town's would-be writer, urges the villagers to let her stay and hide for a while, on condition that Grace repays them with farm work. The townspeople agree, but soon learn that Grace is a wanted fugitive. They want to drive her out, and finally agree that she may stay only if she works even harder.

Grace labours day and night, yet cannot escape misfortune. After a police search, one of the townsmen rapes her. It is the start of something ugly: people begin to humiliate her at will, and even Tom drops his kindly mask. Grace is reduced to the town's dog — working, suffering, her kind heart slowly changing. The townspeople never imagine that the woman's mysterious background will turn today's humiliation into their own downfall.
dogville.bio: Lars von Trier is a Danish director and screenwriter and a co-founder of the Dogme 95 movement. His works include Breaking the Waves, Dancer in the Dark and Melancholia. He constantly changes his narrative and filming methods, putting characters in extreme situations to question the limits of compassion, moral judgment and power.
dogville.st: The film was shot on a soundstage, with lines, words and a few props on the floor marking streets and houses. There are no physical walls, yet characters still knock, talk and hide as usual. This near-theatrical treatment of space lets the audience see several corners at once and directs attention to the relationships between people.
highlights: You can see into every room, and the townspeople still refuse to see what is happening.
Listen to how the residents talk: every demand arrives in the name of help, risk or fairness.

sirat.title: Sirāt
sirat.syn: Amid the booming bass of an underground rave, Luis and his son Esteban cross the desert in search of Mar, his daughter and Esteban's sister, who vanished from a party months ago. As they venture deeper into this scorching, chaotic borderland, facing an unfamiliar freedom and a collapsing order, they search not only for family but for themselves. With documentary-textured long takes and silent gazes, the film builds a spiritual journey about limits, faith and family.
sirat.bio: Oliver Laxe was born in Paris, grew up in Galicia, Spain, and lived and filmed for a long time in Morocco. After You All Are Captains, Mimosas and Fire Will Come, he entered the Cannes main competition with Sirāt, continuing to explore people's place in the natural world and their spiritual experience.
sirat.st: The film sets a search for a missing loved one within rave culture and desert roads, with a score by Kangding Ray. The pounding rhythm of electronic music and the vast landscape form a sharp sensory relationship. Notice how sound changes the sense of distance, and why, the deeper the journey goes, the fewer clues the characters can rely on.
highlights: The opening, with speaker stacks and a crowd, sets the film's physical feel at once; the sound deserves as much attention as the image.
Skip the plot breakdowns if you can, and let the roads, the spaces and what happens to the people stay as sudden as they are.

swordsman.title: Swordsman
swordsman.dir: King Hu / Tsui Hark / Ching Siu-tung / Raymond Lee
swordsman.syn:
The imperial vault's martial arts manual, the Sunflower Manual, has been stolen. Gu Jinfu (Lau Shun), the chief eunuch of the Eastern Depot, leads Ouyang Quan (Jackie Cheung) and others south to investigate the retired Embroidered Guard Lin Zhennan, while also enlisting Zuo Lengchan (Yuen Wah), the self-styled leader of the Five Mountains League, as outside support. Linghu Chong (Sam Hui), senior disciple of the Mount Hua school, and his junior Yue Lingshan (Cecilia Yip) are sent by their master to reinforce Lin, but are too weak to help; after receiving Lin's last testament they flee. Along the way they meet Liu Zhengfeng (Wu Ma), the head of the Shunfeng Hall, Qu Yang (Lam Ching-ying), an elder of the Sun Moon Holy Cult, and Feng Qingyang of the Mount Hua school, who teach them the Xiao Ao Jianghu melody and the Nine Swords of Dugu.

All factions converge on Miao territory for the Sunflower Manual. Ouyang Quan and Zuo Lengchan, unable to settle who deserves the credit, disguise themselves as Lin Pingzhi and infiltrate the Mount Hua party. Linghu Chong befriends Ren Yingying (Cheung Man) and Blue Phoenix (Fennie Yuen) of the Sun Moon Cult, and receives their help through his bond with Qu Yang. When Gu Jinfu and Yue Buqun come to blows over the manual, Linghu Chong, unwilling to see his fellow disciples dragged in, unleashes the Nine Swords of Dugu in anger, and finally grasps the true meaning of “laughing proudly through the jianghu.”
swordsman.bio: King Hu built an important aesthetic for Chinese-language wuxia cinema with works such as Dragon Inn and A Touch of Zen. Tsui Hark is a leading figure of the Hong Kong New Wave who has long reshaped genre cinema through directing, producing and writing. This production brought together different creators and bears the marks of old and new wuxia styles meeting.
swordsman.st: The film was begun by King Hu and completed with the participation of Tsui Hark, Ching Siu-tung, Raymond Lee and others. Rather than staging the full novel, it concentrates on the struggle over the manual, sectarian intrigue and personal choices of staying or leaving. Characters move through landscapes, inns and boats, while the song “Laughing Gaily in the Vast Sea” links the encounters and farewells of the jianghu.
highlights: Linghu Chong and Yue Lingshan make a good pair, and Sam Hui's easy humour gives the film its flavour.
Songs, bamboo groves and boats: beyond the fighting, the film cares about the mood of people meeting.

swordsman.editorial: For entering wuxia through music, characters and jianghu relationships. The hunt for the manual is just the way in; how people find ways of being together outside power is just as worth watching.

swordsman-2.title: Swordsman II
swordsman-2.syn:
Linghu Chong and the Mount Hua disciples prepare to retire from the jianghu, but on the eve of leaving they are once again caught in the strife of the Sun Moon Holy Cult. Dongfang Bubai, who has mastered astonishing martial arts through the Sunflower Manual, faces Ren Woxing, Ren Yingying and others who are trying to take back power in the cult.

Before their positions are clear, Linghu Chong and Dongfang Bubai meet several times in mistaken identity and mutual testing. Personal attraction becomes entangled with conflicts of sect, identity and power, making his wish to leave the jianghu ever harder to fulfil.
swordsman-2.bio: Ching Siu-tung was born in Hong Kong in 1953 and made his name as a martial-arts and action director on films produced or directed by Tsui Hark, such as A Chinese Ghost Story and Swordsman, and later served as action director on Hero. Swordsman II pushed Hong Kong wuxia action design to a peak and is his signature work.
swordsman-2.st:
Produced by Tsui Hark and adapted from Jin Yong’s Swordsman, the film opened in Hong Kong in June 1992 with a gross of about HK$34.46 million, among the year’s top earners, and helped ignite the wave of 1990s Hong Kong wuxia. Its story differs greatly from the novel: Tsui Hark and Ching Siu-tung pushed Dongfang Bubai, a lightly sketched figure in the original, to center stage, played by Brigitte Lin with both menace and tenderness.

By Lin’s own account, Tsui insisted on casting her because of a scene of crazed red-clad abandon she had played in Zu Warriors in 1983. Jin Yong did not approve of such an adaptation, and some media reported he accused Tsui of changing too much. The costume design by Shu Pei Cheung and Yu Ka On won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Costume Design, with multiple other nominations.

The director Wong Jing later said he thought of making Royal Tramp as soon as he saw this film do well, and obtained a print to study for over three hours. The 4K restoration opened in mainland cinemas on October 30, 2026.
highlights: Brigitte Lin’s Dongfang Bubai, menacing and tender, became a classic figure of Chinese wuxia.
Ching Siu-tung’s action design took Hong Kong wuxia to a peak.
The costumes won the Hong Kong Film Award for Best Costume Design at the 12th ceremony.
The 4K restoration is the film’s first mainland theatrical release.

swordsman-2.editorial: For those revisiting or meeting 1990s Hong Kong wuxia for the first time. It departs greatly from Jin Yong’s novel and is best seen as Tsui Hark and Ching Siu-tung’s reinvention; it contains martial-arts fights and killing.

leningrad-cowboys.title: Leningrad Cowboys Go America
leningrad-cowboys.syn: The members of the rock band the Leningrad Cowboys look bizarre: huge sunglasses, towering pompadours and outrageous winklepicker shoes are their trademarks. With no hope of success at home, they decide to try their luck in America. On the eve of departure their bassist freezes to death, but the band still packs him into a wooden crate filled with ice and takes him along. A strange mute from their village secretly follows them to New York. Opportunities in New York are not as plentiful as they imagined, and hard times go on. When they have run out of options, they land a gig at a wedding in Mexico. With their last money they buy a used car from an American salesman and head for Mexico, where their final dream awaits…
leningrad-cowboys.bio: Aki Kaurismäki is a Finnish director and screenwriter, known for The Match Factory Girl, The Man Without a Past, The Other Side of Hope and Fallen Leaves. His films use restrained dialogue, spare compositions and deadpan humor to portray work, wandering and mutual care in hard times.
leningrad-cowboys.st: The film places the band in a fictional American road story, and gave the “Leningrad Cowboys” persona a life beyond the screen. Jim Jarmusch makes a cameo as a used-car dealer. The seemingly unflappable characters, set against a tour that keeps changing places and musical styles, create the film’s distinctive comic rhythm.
highlights: Absurd hair on deadpan faces: most of the jokes need no dialogue.
Each gig is a small culture clash. Watch how the band copes with the next bar.
honors: 获奖｜1989 Finnish Ministry of Education and Culture · State Quality Prize for Film
leningrad-cowboys.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Death and bereavement; Alcohol use. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
leningrad-cowboys.editorial: For fans of deadpan humour and road-trip music. Savour the band's look and its repeated knockbacks, and keep the sense of loss inside the absurdity.

turin-horse.title: The Turin Horse
turin-horse.syn: In 1889, Friedrich Nietzsche witnesses a coachman whipping an old horse, and soon after suffers a mental collapse. What actually happened in Turin, in Nietzsche’s mind, in that horse, and in the desperate daily life of the old coachman and his daughter — no one knows.
turin-horse.bio: Béla Tarr is a Hungarian director known for Sátántangó and Werckmeister Harmonies. Through long collaborations with the writer László Krasznahorkai and with editor and co-director Ágnes Hranitzky, among others, he developed a method of depicting people’s predicaments through black-and-white imagery, long takes and continuous ambient sound.
turin-horse.st: The Turin Horse was co-directed by Tarr and Hranitzky, with cinematography by Fred Kelemen and music by Mihály Víg. Tarr announced it as his last feature. The film compresses its narrative into day-after-day labor, letting the wind, the body and the duration of the shot bear the pressure together.
highlights: The same routines repeat day after day with tiny differences, and the change matters more than the events.
The wind and the recurring score press the world outside into the small house.

turin-horse.editorial: For those who can give themselves to slow repetition and long looking. Changes in daily routine are the key clue; it may be hard to get into when you're tired and rushing, so find a calm frame of mind.

a-better-tomorrow.title: A Better Tomorrow
a-better-tomorrow.syn: Sung Tse-ho (Ti Lung), a key member of a Hong Kong counterfeiting ring, and Mark (Chow Yun-fat) are as close as brothers. During a deal in Taipei, Ho is betrayed by his subordinate Shing (Waise Lee), shot and sent to prison. To avenge his brother, Mark goes to Taiwan alone and is beaten into a cripple; his standing in the underworld plummets, and Ho’s father is soon killed. Sung Tse-kit (Leslie Cheung), who had always idolized his brother, learns Ho’s true identity, comes to hate the underworld and him, and vows to use his position as a police officer to wipe out the gangs. After his release, Ho ignores the advice of Mark, who has waited for him in the hope of rebuilding their glory, and resolves to go straight, but Kit will not forgive him. Meanwhile Shing, now a gang boss, wants Ho to work with him again; when refused, he threatens to harm Kit. Driven into a corner, Ho decides to join Mark once more against a formidable enemy.
a-better-tomorrow.bio: John Woo is a Hong Kong director known for The Killer and Hard Boiled, and for Face/Off after his move to Hollywood. He brought the chivalry, promises and sacrifice of wuxia into modern urban action films, letting gunfights carry strong emotional expression.
a-better-tomorrow.st: Produced by Tsui Hark, the film takes up and rewrites the theme of a gangster trying to start anew from Lung Kong’s 1967 film of the same name. Woo places friendship and family side by side, letting each of the three leads face questions of dignity, responsibility and forgiveness. The force of the action also comes from the emotions these relationships build up.
highlights: Mark's bearing when he's riding high and when he's down and out: dignity isn't spelled out in lines.
Read the pauses and reunions around each shootout together. The action is feeling finally boiling over.

long-live-the-missus.title: Long Live the Missus!
long-live-the-missus.syn: Chen Sizhen (Chiang Tien-liu), a gracious and capable wife, has managed her household relationships well since marrying Tang Zhiyuan (Zhang Fa). One day her brother Chen Sirui (Han Fei) comes from Taiwan to visit Shanghai and meets Zhiyuan’s sister Tang Zhiqin (Wang Yi), and they fall in love at first sight. But Chen’s father (Shi Hui), who refuses to fund Zhiyuan’s plan to start a company, strongly opposes the match. Sizhen has no choice but to lie that the Tang family has gold bars and cash stashed away, and only then does her father agree to finance the company. Once he gets rich, however, Zhiyuan has an affair with his mistress (Shangguan Yunzhu). To protect her husband’s reputation, Sizhen swallows her grievance. Before long Zhiyuan goes bankrupt, the lie is exposed, and the two families fall out. Sizhen finally decides to divorce Zhiyuan, only to run into Sirui and Zhiqin at the lawyer’s office, where they have secretly registered their marriage. Faced with a couple truly in love, where should Sizhen turn?
long-live-the-missus.bio: Sang Hu was an important director at Wenhua Film Company. He worked with Eileen Chang on Unending Love and Long Live the Missus!, and later directed works such as Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai and The New Year’s Sacrifice. He excelled at developing narratives through character relationships and everyday details, so that light comedy keeps the pressure of real-life obligations.
long-live-the-missus.st: Eileen Chang wrote the original screenplay, concentrating the story within the daily work of an ordinary wife keeping family relations together. The film was shot and released in Shanghai in 1947. Besides the dialogue, notice the qipao, the houses and the social occasions: these details are closely tied to the characters’ class positions.
highlights: Every well-meant cover-up causes the next misunderstanding, and Chen Sizhen keeps clearing up after others.
After the laugh, the characters pause for a beat, and the hurt of a family comedy sits in those gaps.
honors: 影史评选｜2005 Hong Kong Film Awards Association · 100 Best Chinese Motion Pictures, No. 82

long-live-the-missus.editorial: For lovers of family comedy and verbal wit. See how the jokes lean on the gendered division of labour at home, while keeping some distance from the attitudes of the time.

bullets-over-broadway.title: Bullets Over Broadway
bullets-over-broadway.syn:
For a long time the playwright David (John Cusack) has led an unfulfilled life, and the purity of an artist leaves him disillusioned with today’s corrupt and chaotic theatre world. To please his mistress Olive (Jennifer Tilly), a mob boss takes a liking to the unknown David’s script and offers to invest, on the condition that David casts Olive in the lead. Though Olive’s nagging and wretched acting drive David mad, he painfully gives in before the money. And so a strange company is born.

The holes in the script, the quarrels among the actresses and the leading man’s ever-growing waistline all fill David with despair, but to his surprise, Cheech (Chazz Palminteri), the bodyguard assigned to watch Olive, unwittingly shows a remarkable gift for writing. With Cheech’s help, the rewritten script becomes a huge success; meanwhile, Cheech’s morbid obsession with the play he has written, and the tangled romances within the company, plunge David into another predicament…
bullets-over-broadway.bio: Woody Allen is an American director, screenwriter and actor, known for Annie Hall, Manhattan, Hannah and Her Sisters and Midnight in Paris. He often writes characters’ self-justification, the unease within relationships and an artistic sensibility into comedy, using dense dialogue to unfold the awkwardness of morality and identity.
bullets-over-broadway.st: The film was co-written by Allen and Douglas McGrath. It turns a play’s path from fundraising to rehearsal into a backstage comedy about talent, credit and compromise. Actors, playwright and backers all claim to be protecting the work, but each understands “art” very differently.
highlights: Watch everyone's reaction each time Cheech rewrites the script: talent turns up in the least respectable person.
Backstage power plays: who pays, who performs and who writes were never cleanly separated.

green-green-grass.title: Green, Green Grass of Home
green-green-grass.syn:
Lu Danian (Kenny Bee) comes to Neiwan to substitute for his sister, who is about to go abroad, and by her arrangement lodges on the upper floor of the home of the primary-school music teacher Chen Suyun (Jiang Ling). Danian becomes head teacher of Class 4 Zhong. In class, he has to deal with the notorious “Three Musketeers” of mischief-makers, while also caring for Zhou Xingwang (Cheng Chuan-wen), a withdrawn student whose parents have divorced.

Chen Suyun is a quiet girl who comes and goes with Danian all day, and the two grow fond of each other. In Neiwan, people catch fish using poison and electric shocks; Danian resolves to end this practice that seriously damages the natural ecology, launching a “protect the river, protect the fish” campaign at Neiwan Primary School and spreading it across the area. Xingwang’s father Zhou Wen (Tsui Fu-sheng) often goes electric fishing, and mocked by classmates for it, the boy runs away from home. Danian and Suyun set out to bring the child back — and will they finally come together?
green-green-grass.bio: Hou Hsiao-hsien is a major director of the Taiwan New Cinema, known for The Boys from Fengkuei, A Time to Live and a Time to Die, A City of Sadness, The Puppetmaster and The Assassin. He often uses distant views, long takes and restrained narration to present personal experience and historical change within family and local life.
green-green-grass.st: This is one of Hou’s early films starring a pop singer, belonging to his early period along with Cute Girl and Cheerful Wind. It keeps a romantic-comedy thread while giving a good deal of time to children, rivers and village life, and is well suited to comparison with his later works.
highlights: Look at what the children do at the edge of the frame. Much of the sense of life comes from beyond the main thread.
The river is a playground, a living environment and a public issue at once.

green-green-grass.contentNote: The available synopsis has been reviewed, but no specific sensitive content has been established. This is not an all-ages assurance or a full content assessment.
green-green-grass.editorial: For lovers of rural daily life and early Hou Hsiao-hsien. Teacher, children and river together form the way in; don't treat the countryside merely as a romantic backdrop.

blood-simple.title: Blood Simple
blood-simple.syn: On a rainy night, Ray (John Getz) and Abby (Frances McDormand) are having an affair at a hotel. Ray is a bartender, while Abby is the wife of the bar’s owner, Marty (Dan Hedaya). Marty suspects his wife of cheating and hires the detective Visser to investigate. Learning the truth, Marty is furious; he sneaks into Ray’s home to kidnap his wife but is hurt in a scuffle. Marty secretly meets Visser and decides to pay him to kill the two. Visser sneaks into Ray’s home and finds Abby’s revolver. On returning, Visser shows Marty a photograph of the two supposedly killed and, taking advantage of his guard being down, shoots him dead. Ray finds Marty’s body and, mistakenly thinking Abby did it, disposes of it. That night Ray returns to the bar and is stunned to find the faked photograph. Neither Ray nor Abby knows the threat of death is closing in step by step…
blood-simple.bio: Joel Coen and Ethan Coen have long co-written and produced films together. Blood Simple was their feature debut, followed by Fargo, The Big Lebowski, No Country for Old Men, Inside Llewyn Davis and more. They excel at interweaving genre storytelling, black humor and characters’ errors of judgment.
blood-simple.st: The film is credited as directed by Joel Coen and produced by Ethan Coen, with both co-writing. Barry Sonnenfeld’s cinematography, Carter Burwell’s score and Frances McDormand’s screen debut already make a distinct presence in this early work. Neon, interior light and sound keep changing what the audience knows.
highlights: Keep track of what we know against what the characters think they know. That gap is where the suspense comes from.
Doors, windows, lighting and off-screen sound tip off the danger before the dialogue does.

blood-simple.editorial: For fans of crime films where misunderstandings pile up. See how much each person knows and what they mistake; the tension also comes from unremarkable details in the space.

spring-in-a-small-town.title: Spring in a Small Town
spring-in-a-small-town.syn:
Around 1948, in an ordinary southern Chinese town where broken walls and ruins are everywhere, the young wife Zhou Yuwen (Wei Wei) lives a dull life with her sickly husband Dai Liyan (Shi Yu). The war has cost Liyan not only his family property but also his faith in life. Yuwen’s days consist of going out in the morning to buy vegetables and fetch Liyan’s medicine, pacing along the town wall for a long while, then returning home despondent; she drops the medicine off with a word or two and spends most of the rest of the day sitting in the room of Liyan’s younger sister Dai Xiu (Zhang Hongmei), embroidering and sighing alone — apart from the wall where she wanders each morning, that room is the only lively place in town for her.

The arrival of Zhang Zhichen (Li Wei) breaks the deathly stillness. He is Liyan’s old friend, and also Yuwen’s former lover. In contrast to Liyan’s gloomy listlessness, Zhichen is young, healthy and full of life, and Dai Xiu, an outsider in this little town, quietly develops feelings for him. But Zhichen has never forgotten Yuwen, and he is undoubtedly what Yuwen longs for and calls to in her heart. As Zhichen and Yuwen play out their psychological game of advancing and retreating, “feelings expressed but restrained by propriety,” Liyan and Dai Xiu glimpse its outline.
spring-in-a-small-town.bio: Fei Mu (1906–1951) was born in Shanghai, received a French education in Beiping, taught himself several languages, joined Lianhua Film Company in 1932 and made his name in 1933 with his directing debut Nocturne of the City. He valued the overall atmosphere of a film, the psychological rhythm of its characters and spatial relations; his works include Human Nature, Blood on Wolf Mountain, Spring in a Small Town and the opera film Sorrows of the Forbidden City’s Heroine. Since the first Pingyao International Film Festival an honour in his name has encouraged new Chinese-language filmmakers; 2026 is the 120th anniversary of his birth.
spring-in-a-small-town.st:
The film organizes feeling through Yuwen’s voice-over, letting what she says of her heart run parallel to the action before our eyes. The story unfolds around a few characters in a limited space, with emotion often expressed through walking, pauses, dissolves and the distance between people. The ruined town wall and house also take part continuously in the changing relationships.

Released in 1948 to a lukewarm response, the film was rediscovered by scholars in the 1980s and is now regarded as a classic of Chinese poetic cinema. The China Film Archive made a 2K restoration in 2014; in 2026 it scanned the original 35mm nitrate negative in 4K and restored it frame by frame, and, after research, fully restored Huang Yijun’s complete score and produced a 5.1 soundtrack. The restoration had its world premiere in September 2026 in TIFF Classics at the 51st Toronto International Film Festival, followed by its Asian premiere as the opening film of the 10th Pingyao International Film Festival.
highlights: Yuwen's voice-over sometimes comes before her actions, sometimes alongside, sometimes out of step. Words and body don't always agree.
The distances between people at doors, windows, corridors and the city wall: restrained gestures carry unquiet feeling.

spring-in-a-small-town.contentNote: Available story information indicates: Illness, treatment or care; Relationship conflict or coercion. Detailed depiction and intensity have not been verified; consider your individual needs.
spring-in-a-small-town.editorial: For those who'll read feeling in restrained dialogue and everyday action. The postwar ruins and courtyard aren't decoration; what the characters can't say is especially worth watching.

mon-oncle.title: Mon Oncle
mon-oncle.syn: Monsieur Hulot (Jacques Tati) comes from the countryside to stay with his sister (Adrienne Servantie) in Paris. He cannot get used to the modern appliances in her home and is constantly thrown into a flap. Fortunately, his young nephew Gérard likes this uncle and goes everywhere with him; Gérard likewise dislikes the modern gadgets at home, so Hulot takes him to play at an old house in the suburbs. Hulot’s brother-in-law, Monsieur Arpel (Jean-Pierre Zola), finds him a job at his factory, but Hulot cannot adapt to modern machinery either, botches many things and causes many laughs. Fed up, his brother-in-law decides to send him off with another job elsewhere, and Hulot happily says goodbye to his nephew, taking it as the end of an unusual holiday…
mon-oncle.bio: Jacques Tati was a French director, actor and comedic creator best known for the screen character Monsieur Hulot. His works include Monsieur Hulot’s Holiday, Mon Oncle and Playtime. His comedy relies on physical movement, spatial staging and sound, turning everyday settings into a stage that rewards patient observation.
mon-oncle.st: This was Tati’s first feature in color and the second Monsieur Hulot film. It contrasts the modern house, the factory and the old quarter, with sound design and composition carrying a great deal of the humor. You needn’t watch only the lead: a figure deep in the frame or off to the side may be completing a small comedy of their own.
highlights: The fountain, the footsteps and the machines often announce how absurd the environment is before the characters do.
Don't just watch the centre. Tati often puts several gags into one space, and the edges and background count.
honors: 获奖｜1958 Cannes Film Festival · Special Jury Prize

mon-oncle.contentNote: The available synopsis has been reviewed, but no specific sensitive content has been established. This is not an all-ages assurance or a full content assessment.
mon-oncle.editorial: For fans of visual comedy and the design of living space. Put aside the habit of chasing plot and see how a house, machines and sound make daily life funny.

where-is-the-friends-house.title: Where Is the Friend’s House?
where-is-the-friends-house.syn: In a primary school in a remote Iranian mountain village, a group of children listen to their teacher in class. While checking homework, the teacher finds that Mohammad Reza has repeatedly failed to complete his, and scolds him severely, saying he will be expelled if it happens again. The teacher stresses that this is to help them build good discipline. After school, the little boy Ahmad discovers that he has taken his seatmate Mohammad’s notebook home by mistake. Having understood the teacher’s earnest admonition, Ahmad knows this notebook is Mohammad’s proof of being able to continue in class. To return the notebook, Ahmad hopes his mother and grandfather will help, but both fail him. So he can only set out alone to the village in the mountains across the way to find his seatmate. But since he does not know where his friend lives, he meets obstacles everywhere and encounters unimaginable difficulties…
where-is-the-friends-house.bio: Abbas Kiarostami was an Iranian director and screenwriter whose works include Close-Up, Taste of Cherry and The Wind Will Carry Us. Where Is the Friend’s House?, together with And Life Goes On and Through the Olive Trees, forms the “Koker trilogy,” which revisits the same place and way of life in different ways.
where-is-the-friends-house.st: The film is the starting point of the Koker trilogy, following a child’s search for the owner of a notebook through a single day. It does not advance on a complex plot; instead, roads, questions, waiting and repeatedly going the wrong way build tension. In the process, the rules of the adult world reveal their distance from the child’s sense of responsibility.
highlights: Do the adults ever really answer the boy? Failed communication is more maddening than outright refusal.
Hill paths, doors and corners keep coming back, and the terrain turns a small errand into an adventure.

the-sacrifice.title: The Sacrifice
the-sacrifice.syn: The critic Alexander (Erland Josephson) celebrates his fiftieth birthday at his home in Sweden; his young son, who has just had throat surgery, cannot speak. In silence, the two plant a sapling, hoping it will sprout green branches. But that same evening, the radio broadcasts news of a nuclear missile launch: the Third World War is about to break out. In despair Alexander prays to God that war not happen, even vowing to give up everything he has to stop the apocalypse. Longing for the world to be reborn, and in a state of utter exhaustion, Alexander sets fire to his own house. Amid the roaring blaze, he is taken to hospital by ambulance. His young son goes to the shore to keep watering the sapling they planted together, and everything seems calm again.
the-sacrifice.bio: Andrei Tarkovsky was a Soviet director whose seven feature films include Ivan’s Childhood, Andrei Rublev, Solaris, Mirror, Stalker, Nostalghia and The Sacrifice. He also wrote Sculpting in Time, and explored human spiritual life through sustained shots, natural elements and spaces of memory.
the-sacrifice.st: The Sacrifice is Tarkovsky’s last feature, shot in Sweden with cinematography by Sven Nykvist and starring Erland Josephson. The film sets one day in a family against questions about destruction, faith and giving, and many key passages unfold through the characters’ movement and long periods of waiting.
highlights: Where characters stand, indoors or in the landscape, matters; even a distant movement can shift a whole scene.
Read the dead tree, the child and the recurring sound together: promises in this film continue through concrete acts.

the-sacrifice.editorial: For those ready to enter questions of faith and responsibility. Space, waiting and a sense of ritual in the long takes matter; don't squeeze it between two rushed screenings.

faces-places.title: Faces Places
faces-places.syn: Agnès Varda, the “grandmother of the French New Wave,” and the street artist JR travel through the villages of France in a small van. Along the way they photograph the people they meet, then paste billboard-sized portraits onto the walls of houses and factories.
faces-places.bio: Agnès Varda was a French film director and visual artist whose works include Cléo from 5 to 7, Vagabond and The Gleaners and I. JR is a French artist known for giant photographic projects in public spaces. This film lets cinema and street photography join together in looking at ordinary people.
faces-places.st: In their Cannes interview, the two explained that the collaboration began as nothing more than a short rural film project, and then kept extending as encounters accumulated. They did not write the plot in advance, but first chose a place or a theme, then let the people and events on site shape the shooting. The easy conversation in the film also comes from this way of working together.
highlights: Once the giant photographs go up, how do the subjects see their own faces and surroundings anew?
The two artists tease and watch each other, and eventually become the ones being recorded.

faces-places.editorial: For fans of meetings between people and public art. Beyond how the giant portraits are made, how ordinary people respond to being seen is just as moving, and you can set it against your own city.

john-wick.title: John Wick
john-wick.syn:
John Wick, a top assassin retired for years, has just lost his wife, who left him a puppy before her death to help him through the hardest days. The son of a Russian crime boss covets his sports car, breaks into his home, beats him up, takes the car and kills the puppy.

John, who once struck fear into the whole underworld, picks up his guns again. For a dog and a promise, he fights his way through the gang’s nightclub, church and docks, and the Continental Hotel, a sanctuary built for assassins, opens its doors to the audience for the first time.
john-wick.bio: Chad Stahelski, born in 1968, came up through martial arts and stunt work, and was Keanu Reeves’s stunt double on The Matrix. In 1997 he and David Leitch founded the action-design and stunt-training company 87Eleven, and for years they worked as stunt coordinators and second-unit directors. John Wick was the first feature the two moved into directing together; under a Directors Guild ruling only Stahelski is credited as director, with Leitch listed as a producer. Stahelski went on to direct the later main entries in the series and set up 87Eleven Entertainment to carry action design into larger productions.
john-wick.st:
The script was written by Derek Kolstad around 2012 under the title Scorn, after he had written dozens of scripts that never got made. The original protagonist was a retired killer close to old age, closer in spirit to the 1967 film Point Blank. After reading it, Keanu Reeves brought it to his longtime stunt collaborators Stahelski and Leitch. Reeves always referred to the project by the hero’s name, and the title became John Wick; the character’s age was also adjusted to fit Reeves, who was 49 at the time.

It was produced by Basil Iwanyk’s Thunder Road Pictures and distributed by Summit Entertainment. The two new directors raised the body count, the amount of action and the mythology of the assassins’ underworld, and details such as the hotel, the gold coins and the rules were added during shooting and post-production. Much of the action uses medium shots and longer takes, with the actors trained to perform the gunplay and close-quarters fighting themselves, so the audience can see each reload and disarm.

Released in the United States in October 2014 on a modest budget, it became a turning point in Reeves’s career and the start of a long-running series. It had not previously played in mainland Chinese cinemas; this is the first time the series’ opening film reaches the mainland big screen.
highlights: The script began as Scorn, about an aging killer; Keanu Reeves changed the title and the character’s age.
Both directors came from stunt work, so gunplay, falls and reloads are staged in clear view.
The hotel, the gold coins and the no-killing-inside-the-hotel rule start the world of the whole series here.
Made on a modest budget, it became a turning point for Reeves and launched a long-running series.
john-wick.contentNote: Also informed by a published overseas content advisory. The running time and cut may differ from this screening; consider your individual needs.
john-wick.editorial: Choose it to watch action staging on a big screen: how space, bodies and gunplay link one beat to the next. The revenge begins with the killing of the hero’s dog, so viewers sensitive to animal harm should think first.

happy-birthday.title: Happy Birthday
happy-birthday.syn:
Eight-year-old Toha works as a child maid in a wealthy household in Cairo. She has grown up with the employers’ daughter Nelly and become her closest playmate. Nelly’s birthday is near, and Toha, who has never had a birthday herself, is determined to throw her the perfect party, as if it might give her a share of happiness too.

As she grows closer to Nelly’s mother Layla, the line between master and servant begins to blur. But the nearer the party gets, the more clearly Toha realizes that she belongs neither to this family nor to this party. The whole story takes place within a single day.
happy-birthday.bio: Sarah Goher was raised in the South Bronx by Egyptian immigrant parents and works as an Egyptian-American director and screenwriter; she has worked on Marvel’s series Moon Knight. Happy Birthday is her feature debut, co-written with the director Mohamed Diab. It had its world premiere at the 2025 Tribeca Festival and won Best International Narrative Feature, Best International Screenplay and the Nora Ephron Award, later added the FIPRESCI first-feature prize at Palm Springs, and was Egypt’s submission for the 98th Academy Awards’ Best International Feature.
happy-birthday.st:
The film follows eight-year-old Toha, a child maid for a wealthy Cairo family who becomes friends with her employer’s daughter, Nelly. Learning that Nelly has never truly had a birthday party, she resolves to give her friend an unforgettable one, and the story unfolds through the preparations. The director hands the story to a child’s point of view: kitchen, living room and party are entirely different worlds inside the same house, and class lines emerge through which rooms Toha may enter and what she may touch.

Lead actress Doha Ramadan is a newcomer, and her performance was singled out in Tribeca’s and several other festivals’ write-ups. Nelly Karim, Hanan Motawie and Hanan Youssef also appear. The cinematographer is Seif El Din Khaled and the editor Ahmed Hafez; the producers include Jamie Foxx.

The film was in Tribeca’s International Narrative Competition, then opened El Gouna Film Festival out of competition and won its audience award; it went on to take the Heartland Film Festival Grand Jury Prize, the São Paulo International Film Festival’s Best Performance and Mill Valley’s audience prize, making it one of the most-awarded debuts of the 2025 festival season.
highlights: Eight-year-old Toha is both a child worker and a child who wants to throw her friend a party, and the film stays at her eye level.
Doha Ramadan, a newcomer, was singled out by several festivals; São Paulo gave her Best Performance.
Three Tribeca awards plus honors from Palm Springs, Heartland, Mill Valley and El Gouna.
Egypt’s submission for the 98th Academy Awards’ Best International Feature.
