rosetta.title: Rosetta
rosetta.syn: Young Rosetta lives in a trailer park with her alcoholic mother. She searches desperately for work, hoping to escape poverty through her own labour and lead an ordinary life like everyone else. Repeated dismissals and rejections put that simple wish out of reach. When a young man offers help, the pressure to survive pushes her into a hard choice. The film follows her footsteps, portraying a girl's stubborn pursuit of work, dignity and belonging.
rosetta.bio: Belgian brothers Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne began in documentary and have long explored work, poverty and individual moral choices. Following La Promesse, Rosetta developed their camera's close attention to bodies and actions, earning them their first Palme d'Or.
rosetta.st: Premiered in competition at Cannes on 22 May 1999 and won the Palme d'Or by a unanimous jury decision the next day. Émilie Dequenne shared the Best Actress award for her screen debut and later received a César nomination for Most Promising Actress in 2000. The camera stays close to Rosetta's movements and breathing, making her search for work a physical experience. Repeated tasks—finding a job, carrying water and moving gas cylinders—bind the need to survive to the desire for dignity.
honors: 获奖｜1999 52nd Cannes Film Festival · Palme d'Or (unanimous jury decision)
获奖｜1999 52nd Cannes Film Festival · Best Actress (Émilie Dequenne, shared)
提名｜2000 25th César Awards · Most Promising Actress (Émilie Dequenne)
获奖｜1999 Belgian Film Critics Association · André Cavens Award for Best Belgian Film
warnings: Physical struggles with police and an employer
rosetta.editorial: For viewers interested in labour, young women's lives and the Dardennes' filmmaking. Follow Rosetta's movements and search for work before judging her troubling choices: compassion and moral discomfort coexist here. The close handheld camera and relentless anxiety make this an intense viewing experience.
highlights: A camera close to the body: Following Rosetta's shoulders, steps and breathing limits our view of the world. Social pressure is felt physically before its wider structures come into focus.
Work and dignity: Job hunting, fetching water and carrying gas cylinders recur throughout. Work becomes her gateway to an ordinary life, entangling survival with moral choices.
Performance through action: Dequenne's tense physical presence carries the story. The film neither rushes to explain Rosetta's psychology nor turns her into an easily lovable symbol of poverty.

ponette.title: Ponette
ponette.syn: Four-year-old Ponette loses her mother in a car crash that also injures her. She cannot grasp what death means and will not accept that her mother is gone for good. Her father, relatives and little friends try to comfort her in their own ways, but no explanation dispels her confusion and longing. Convinced her mother will return, she keeps talking to her, prays to God, and searches for reunion with a child's imagination and stubbornness. Between reality and fantasy, she travels alone through loss, faith and growing up.
ponette.bio: Jacques Doillon is a French writer and director, born in Paris in 1944. His films frequently explore children, adolescents and the conflicts within close relationships. Known for The Little Gangster and Ponette, he builds emotional drama from small changes in speech, gesture and behaviour.
ponette.st:
Ponette screened in competition at the 53rd Venice Film Festival in September 1996, where Victoire Thivisol won the Volpi Cup for Best Actress and the film received the FIPRESCI Prize. Its precise first screening date remains unconfirmed. It opened in France on 25 September 1996.

Before completing the screenplay, Doillon spoke with young children about death and their mothers. A child psychoanalyst followed the performers during production. The film draws on children's own ways of speaking and understanding: religious explanations, playground exchanges and stubborn hope coexist without resolving neatly into an adult lesson.

The camera frequently stays close to the children's eye level, treating play, silence and imagination as meaningful emotional actions. ACMI highlights this perspective and the performances that sustain it. Roger Ebert awarded the film 3.5 out of four stars. Production footage later became Jeanne Crépeau's separate Canadian documentary Playing Ponette (2007); that film's title and production details should not be confused with this feature.
honors: 入围｜1996 Venice Film Festival · Main Competition
获奖｜1996 Venice Film Festival · Volpi Cup for Best Actress (Victoire Thivisol)
获奖｜1996 Venice Film Festival · FIPRESCI Prize

获奖｜1997 New York Film Critics Circle · Best Foreign Language Film
ponette.editorial: For viewers drawn to a child's perspective and finely observed performances. Notice how Ponette keeps asking, waiting and playing as she searches for her own way to understand loss. The story concerns a young child's grief after her mother's death and can be emotionally demanding.
highlights: A child’s questions make the experience of loss immediate and difficult to dismiss.
Victoire Thivisol moves delicately between playfulness and grief.
Conversations about death and faith turn abstract questions into actions children can understand.

amour-2012.title: Amour
amour-2012.syn: Georges and Anne are retired music teachers in their eighties, living together in their Paris apartment. An illness gradually weakens Anne and changes their daily life completely. Honouring his wife's wish not to return to hospital, Georges takes on the burden of care alone. As ageing, pain and loss close in, the couple must face the hardest test love can bring.
amour-2012.bio: Michael Haneke is an Austrian writer and director, born in Munich in 1942. After working in theatre and television, he developed a rigorous cinema of violence, spectatorship and intimate relationships. Both The White Ribbon and Amour won the Palme d’Or. Here, his precise observation centres on the daily life of an elderly couple.
amour-2012.st:
Amour had its world premiere in competition at the 65th Cannes Film Festival on 20 May 2012 and won the Palme d’Or. In 2013 it received the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film, alongside nominations for Best Picture, Director, Actress and Original Screenplay. It also won five César Awards: Film, Director, Actor, Actress and Original Screenplay.

At Cannes, Haneke described his starting point as the difficulty of facing the suffering of someone one loves. He was posing a question rather than supplying a solution to ageing. He conceived Georges for Jean-Louis Trintignant, with Emmanuelle Riva and Isabelle Huppert completing the central family. Pianist Alexandre Tharaud also appears.

Long takes and the enclosed apartment make physical change, silence and the labour of care central to the drama. The film avoids easy reassurance. Critical responses particularly praised the leading performances; Amy Taubin highlighted the precision of the filmmaking and the delicacy of the acting.

获奖｜2013 Academy Awards · Best Foreign Language Film

amour-2012.editorial: For viewers interested in performance, intimate relationships and the ethics of care. Notice the couple’s surviving humour, courtesy and shared habits: they make their predicament painfully specific. The film addresses stroke, loss of independence, end-of-life care and death, with a slow pace and considerable emotional weight.
highlights: Two veteran performers convey decades of shared life through small gestures.
The familiar apartment gradually becomes a boundary around care and solitude.
Love is examined through everyday responsibility and unresolved ethical questions.

les-miserables-2019.title: Les Misérables
les-miserables-2019.syn: Stéphane joins the anti-crime squad in Montfermeil, a Paris suburb, patrolling with two veteran colleagues. He soon sees the tense, fragile balance between residents, local powers and the police. While tracking a stolen lion cub, an officer wounds a boy, and a drone captures it all. The struggle over that footage lets long-simmering tensions in the neighbourhood slip out of control.
les-miserables-2019.bio: Ladj Ly is a French filmmaker born in 1978. Beginning with documentaries and shorts, he has long filmed the Clichy–Montfermeil neighbourhood where he grew up, working with collaborators including artist JR. His 2017 short Les Misérables became the basis of this first fiction feature, bringing an insider’s perspective to the tensions between policing and neighbourhood life.
les-miserables-2019.st:
Les Misérables premiered in competition at the 72nd Cannes Film Festival on 15 May 2019, sharing the Jury Prize with Bacurau. It subsequently received an Academy Award nomination for Best International Feature Film and won four César Awards in 2020: Film, Male Newcomer, Editing and the Public Award.

Developed from Ly’s 2017 short of the same name, the feature was inspired by an incident of police violence he had filmed. It was shot in the Paris suburb where he grew up. Its title echoes the setting and social concerns of Victor Hugo’s novel, rather than adapting its plot.

A patrol gradually exposes competing neighbourhood interests before everyday friction escalates into confrontation. Ground-level footage and drone images shift the viewer’s position, making evidence and control of the image crucial. Cannes’s introduction emphasised Ly’s attention to residents and police; Time praised the film’s ability to immerse viewers in its world. Reviews also noted its accumulating energy and explosive final act.

Watch how the same encounter looks to officers, teenagers and witnesses, and how recording an image changes the balance of power. highlights: A new officer’s first patrol gradually reveals the neighbourhood’s competing powers.
A drone turns questions of evidence and ownership of images into a central visual theme.

anatomy-of-a-fall.title: Anatomy of a Fall
anatomy-of-a-fall.syn: Writer Sandra lives in the French Alps with her husband Samuel and their visually impaired son Daniel. One day Samuel is found dead below their chalet, and Sandra becomes the prime suspect. As the investigation and trial proceed, the couple's quarrels, their creative rivalry and the secrets of family life come out one by one. Daniel, both a boy who has lost his father and a key witness, must choose between memory, doubt and trust in his mother.
anatomy-of-a-fall.bio: French filmmaker Justine Triet explores the friction between private lives and public judgment. Her features include Age of Panic, In Bed with Victoria and Sibyl. Her fourth feature, Anatomy of a Fall, was co-written with Arthur Harari.
anatomy-of-a-fall.st: World premiere: Cannes Competition, 21 May 2023; winner of the Palme d’Or. Triet and Harari developed the screenplay over three years, consulting a criminal lawyer. She wrote Sandra for Hüller and withheld the ending from the young actor to preserve his uncertainty. Budget constraints led to shooting with an Alexa and vintage lenses rather than 35mm film.

anatomy-of-a-fall.editorial: For viewers who enjoy courtroom drama and ambiguous characters. Listen to how testimony turns shared memories into competing narratives. Language, recordings and the child’s perspective complicate every judgment. The long, dialogue-driven film rewards patience.
highlights: Marriage, creative work and the unequal division of time enter the courtroom.
Recordings and offscreen sound become evidence.
Hüller, Arlaud and Machado-Graner keep the legal suspense rooted in family life.

parallel-tales.title: Parallel Tales
parallel-tales.syn: Novelist Sylvie begins secretly watching the neighbour across from her in search of inspiration for a new book. She hires a young man, Adam, to help with her daily life, never imagining that this stranger will transform her life and her writing. As relationships shift, the fiction she writes and her real life interweave and the once-clear boundary blurs, until the imagined story outruns everyone's reality.
parallel-tales.bio: Iranian filmmaker Asghar Farhadi builds moral dilemmas from ordinary events and conflicting accounts. A Separation and The Salesman won Oscars for Foreign Language Film. Parallel Tales returns him to France after The Past, turning his attention to the relationship between imagination and everyday life.
parallel-tales.st: World premiere: Cannes Competition, 14 May 2026, alongside its French theatrical release. Later festival appearances include Sydney, AFI FEST and Hamburg. Loosely inspired by Kieślowski’s Dekalog: Six, it places a novelist opposite a group of film foley artists. Young assistant Adam connects their apartments as writing, sound effects and dual identities blur reality and fiction.
honors: 入围｜2026 Cannes Film Festival · Competition (Palme d’Or)
入围｜2026 Sydney Film Festival · Official Competition
parallel-tales.editorial: For viewers intrigued by voyeurism and narrative puzzles. Festival programmers praise its imaginative maze; several premiere reviews found its structure more convincing than its characters. Watch how observing others changes their lives.
highlights: Huppert leads an ensemble with several dual roles.
Foley work questions how realism is manufactured.
A novelist’s curiosity becomes an ethical dilemma.
parallel-tales.contentNote: Based on published synopses and distribution materials: Voyeurism and boundary-crossing; Emotional manipulation and betrayal. Not a full viewing review; intensity, flashing and sound levels remain unverified. This is not an official classification.

and-the-spring-comes.title: And the Spring Comes
and-the-spring-comes.syn:
In a steel town in northern China in the 1980s, Wang Cailing (Jiang Wenli) is an older middle-school music teacher, plain-looking but convinced that her voice is made for opera. She is determined to put down roots in Beijing and refuses to live an ordinary life like everyone around her.

The steelworker Zhou Yu (Wu Guohua) falls for her voice on the radio and courts her under the pretext of becoming her pupil; she falls instead for her cousin Huang Sibao (Li Guangjie), who longs to study at an art academy in Beijing but keeps failing the exams. She then meets Mr Hu (Jiao Gang), a man obsessed with ballet since childhood and treated as an oddity, and Gao Beibei (Zhang Yao), who claims to be seriously ill and asks for help entering a young singers’ competition. Each time she nears her dream, reality pushes her back. As spring approaches and the wind turns damp and mild, her ambition, pride and loneliness swell together.
and-the-spring-comes.bio: Gu Changwei, born in Xi’an in 1957, is one of the most important cinematographers of China’s Fifth Generation, having shot films for directors including Chen Kaige and Zhang Yimou. He turned to directing with Peacock (2005), which won a Silver Bear at the 55th Berlin International Film Festival. And the Spring Comes is his second film as director and continues his collaboration with screenwriter Li Qiang on small-town stories. His directing keeps a cinematographer’s sensitivity: he looks at ordinary faces and spaces for a long time without hurrying to judge.
and-the-spring-comes.st:
And the Spring Comes was directed by Gu Changwei and written by Li Qiang, their second feature together after Peacock. It is again set in a small northern town in the 1980s and focuses on someone who is misunderstood yet refuses to give up. Wang Cailing’s voice-over, delivered in the Baotou dialect, sets a tone from the opening of self-pity and self-mockery intertwined, and the film’s comedy and sorrow often spring from the same place.

Jiang Wenli visibly gained weight and changed her appearance for the role, and said in interviews that she hoped audiences would see the character rather than the star. The steel town, the loudspeaker broadcasts and Italian opera are set against one another, so that a woman destined to be overlooked is placed against her ‘elevated’ aspirations.

In October 2007 the film premiered in competition at the 2nd Rome Film Festival, where Jiang Wenli won Best Actress. It opened in mainland China in April 2008. Critical reaction was mixed: some reviewers found the central character hard to reach and the film somewhat even-tempered, while others praised the nuance of Jiang’s performance.
honors: 获奖｜2007 Rome Film Festival (2nd) · Best Actress (Jiang Wenli)
入选｜2007 Rome Film Festival (2nd) · Main competition
and-the-spring-comes.editorial: Suited to viewers interested in performance and small-town storytelling. Notice the gap between Wang Cailing’s singing and monologues and the silence of those around her; the film offers her no easy exit. It includes mockery of appearance and identity and characters’ extreme choices in despair; the mood is heavy.
highlights: Jiang Wenli transforms herself through body, voice and accent, and won Best Actress at Rome.
The town’s spaces, loudspeakers and opera create a contrast that makes aspiration both comic and sincere.
Continues the Peacock team, putting the ‘superfluous person’ of the 1980s small town at the centre of the screen; its Douban rating is 8.4 from over 170,000 ratings.
After the Rome premiere, Variety and Screen International each commented on the central character and Jiang’s performance, with mixed views of the film overall.
and-the-spring-comes.contentNote: Compiled from public synopses and release materials; involves appearance-based humiliation and exclusion, and suicide-related content. Not fully screened; intensity, flashing and volume are not verified, and this is not an official rating.

crows-and-sparrows.title: Crows and Sparrows
crows-and-sparrows.syn:
Winter 1948. With the outcome of the Huaihai Campaign decided, Nationalist officials in Shanghai are in a panic. Hou Yibo (Li Tianji), a section chief in the Ministry of Defence, has seized a house in an alley, installed his mistress Yu Xiaoying (Huang Zongying) upstairs, and let the rooms to the schoolteacher Hua Jiezhi (Sun Daolin) and his family, to the stallholder Boss Xiao, nicknamed ‘Little Broadcast’ (Zhao Dan), and his wife, and to the original owner, the old newspaper proofreader Kong Youwen (Wei Heling).

As the situation worsens, Hou plans to sell the house and evict everyone for a last profit. The tenants have their own schemes: the teacher looks for another way out, Little Broadcast and his wife gamble on gold, and the old owner can only swallow his anger. Price spikes, runs on gold, student strikes and the arrest of teachers press in one after another until the tenants realise that without solidarity they will simply be thrown out.
crows-and-sparrows.bio: Zheng Junli (1911–1969) was a Chinese film director, actor, screenwriter and film theorist. He began in Shanghai theatre and cinema and in 1947 co-directed Spring River Flows East with Cai Chusheng, a high point of 1940s Chinese cinema. In 1949 he directed Crows and Sparrows, an ensemble comedy about people on the eve of a historical turn. His later films, including Lin Zexu and Withered Tree Blooms Again, continued his attention to history and reality. He also wrote The Birth of a Character, summarising his experience of acting and creation.
crows-and-sparrows.st:
Crows and Sparrows was produced by Kunlun Film Company. Its origin lies in a gathering in Shanghai at the end of 1948, where Chen Baichen, Shen Fu, Zheng Junli, Chen Liting, Zhao Dan and others discussed making a film that would record the last days of the Nationalist regime while expressing filmmakers’ hope for a new world. Working around the metaphor of ‘crows’ and ‘sparrows’, they quickly arrived at an outline; Chen Baichen wrote the script and Zheng Junli directed. The film was shot as the Nationalist government collapsed and finished and released after the liberation of Shanghai.

The film compresses its world into a single alley house and uses a small ‘community of tenants’ to reflect a whole era. Zhao Dan’s ‘Little Broadcast’, righteous yet petty and forever dreaming of getting rich, is vivid as a Shanghai townsman; Shangguan Yunzhu, Wu Yin, Sun Daolin, Wei Heling and other stars of the day each hold their own corner of the ensemble, which is full of rhythm and satire. Some scholars note that the optimism of the ending bears the mark of the historical turn during which it was made.

In 2024 the Shanghai Film Dubbing Studio released a Shanghainese-dubbed version of the film as part of its ‘Classic Renewal’ series. This screening is the 4K restoration.
honors: 获奖｜1957 Ministry of Culture · Outstanding Film Award, First Prize
获奖｜1957 Ministry of Culture · Outstanding Film Individual Award, First Prize (Zhao Dan)
获奖｜1986 France’s 1st ‘Keluomiyi’ International Film Festival (as named in Chinese sources) · Recommended Film Award
crows-and-sparrows.editorial: Suited to viewers interested in Chinese film history, ensemble acting and social satire. Watch how Little Broadcast’s speculation, the teacher’s helplessness and the landlord’s bullying carry the pressure of a great era into the details of one house. It depicts political oppression of the time, and its narration and dialogue are strongly of their era.
highlights: Zhao Dan’s ‘Little Broadcast’ remains one of the liveliest urban characters on the Chinese screen.
One house and a few families compress the social panorama on the eve of collapse into an ensemble comedy.
A collective work by Kunlun’s left-leaning filmmakers: an outline born at a dinner table, written by Chen Baichen, directed by Zheng Junli.
The sparrows stand for ordinary citizens and the crows for the rulers; the later ‘Kill the Sparrows’ campaign added a layer of historical irony to the metaphor.
crows-and-sparrows.contentNote: Compiled from public synopses and release materials; involves political oppression, arrest and execution, and a child’s serious illness. Not fully screened; intensity, flashing and volume are not verified, and this is not an official rating.

clayface.title: Clayface
clayface.syn:
Matt Hagen rises from the streets of Gotham to become a Hollywood actor, until a brutal attack leaves him disfigured and his career collapses. An experimental treatment promises to restore the life he lost.

His face recovers, but his body and his grasp on reality begin to change. As he turns toward revenge, the ability to reshape himself puts his identity at risk.
clayface.bio:
British writer-director James Watkins works across psychological horror, thrillers and crime. His early writing credits include My Little Eye and Gone. He wrote and directed his first feature, Eden Lake (2008), followed by the Gothic horror film The Woman in Black (2012) and the action thriller The Take (2016).

His television work includes Black Mirror’s Shut Up and Dance, McMafia and The Ipcress File. He also wrote and directed the English-language Speak No Evil (2024). Seen together, these works offer a useful route into Clayface: familiar social spaces gradually become places from which characters cannot escape.
clayface.st:
DC Studios and 6th & Idaho produced the Warner Bros. release, based on DC characters. Mike Flanagan supplied the story and shares screenplay credit with Hossein Amini; James Watkins directed. Producers are Matt Reeves, Lynn Harris, James Gunn and Peter Safran. The creative team includes cinematographer Rob Hardy, editor Jon Harris, costume designer Keith Madden and composer Volker Bertelmann.

Watkins cited David Cronenberg’s The Fly as an important reference: physical change becomes disturbing because an identifiable person is at its center. For an actor, losing his face also means losing an instrument of work and a public identity. The treatment can therefore be read as a bargain over the cost of remaining oneself.

The Gotham design drew on 1970s New York street photography and 1930s cinema, with older lenses reducing the smoothness of digital images. Watch how the city’s surfaces and constricted spaces reflect Matt’s situation.

For the airplane bathroom sequence shown in the trailer, Watkins described a moving cabin set and prosthetic eye makeup. The scene offers a way to notice how practical movement and an actor’s physical responses make transformation feel tangible.

The world premiere took place at the Hollywood Legion Theater in Los Angeles on October 13, 2026. International theatrical releases began October 21, followed by North America on October 23 and Mainland China on November 27. The premiere was not a festival selection or award; no festival competition or award record was verified by November 17. The Mainland theatrical runtime is the same as the international version, listed at 109 minutes.
clayface.editorial: For viewers interested in body horror, screen performance and anxiety about appearance. Start with what Matt is willing to sacrifice to reclaim his life, then consider how revenge and transformation alter that wish. The basic story does not require prior DC viewing. Reactions differ on the depth of characterization; viewers sensitive to disfigurement, injury or medical imagery should read the content notes first.
highlights: Watch the face as an actor’s working instrument: mirrors, other people’s looks and a public image can shape Matt’s sense of self.
The Fly makes a useful companion film for comparing physical transformation with a human tragedy.
Older lenses and street-photography references offer a route into Gotham’s texture, shadows and constricting spaces.
Tom Rhys Harries plays Matt Hagen; Naomi Ackie joins the experimental-treatment story. Notice how performance connects character and transformation effects.
For a director introduction, pair Eden Lake, The Woman in Black and the 2024 English-language Speak No Evil: fear develops in three different environments.
Reception is divided: Rotten Tomatoes shows 78% positive critics and 94% verified audiences, while MTC is 58/100. Approval percentages and average scores measure different things.
warnings: Strong bloody violence and injury detail
Disfigurement, bodily transformation and medical procedures
Strong language, nudity and sexual references
clayface.contentNote: Based on UK BBFC theatrical advice and the US release classification: strong bloody violence, injury and medical detail, disfigurement, bodily transformation, threat, strong language, nudity, sexual references, drug use and verbal references to sexual violence. The UK cinema version carries a flashing-image warning for photosensitive viewers. The US theatrical version is MPA R, not a Mainland classification. The supplied Mainland poster advises caution for minors. The Mainland theatrical runtime matches the international version; specific editing and sensory differences remain unverified.

dune-2021.title: Dune
dune-2021.syn:
In a distant future, spice sustains interstellar travel and imperial power, yet it is found only on the desert planet Arrakis. House Atreides is ordered to take control of the planet. Young Paul arrives with Duke Leto and his mother Jessica, unaware of how deeply this apparent honor is entangled in political bargains and an old enemy’s plans.

Paul dreams of the desert and a Fremen girl. His mother’s training, his unusual perceptions and the prophecies surrounding him remain difficult to understand. When catastrophe strikes the family, mother and son must enter the desert to survive. Adapting the first half of the novel, this opening film establishes the ecology, interests and dangers of its world.
dune-2021.bio:
Born in Quebec, Canada, in 1967, Denis Villeneuve began in French-language shorts and features. Incendies (2010) turns a family investigation toward the scars of war. Prisoners and Enemy (both 2013) explore moral uncertainty and unstable identity, while Sicario (2015) builds tension through space, rhythm and offscreen danger.

Arrival (2016) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) brought these concerns into science fiction: unfamiliar languages and monumental architecture remain connected to memory, perception and fate. His Dune films continue that interest through sound, scale and a restricted human viewpoint. Notice the pauses, distant figures and sudden threats that make a world felt before it is fully explained.
dune-2021.st:
Frank Herbert’s 1965 novel places planetary ecology, resources, religion and empire in one system. Jon Spaihts, Denis Villeneuve and Eric Roth adapted it for the screen. Dividing the first novel into two films allowed more room for family relationships and Arrakis; this installment does not complete Paul’s journey.

Cinematographer Greig Fraser and production designer Patrice Vermette built a tangible world through sets in Hungary and locations in Jordan, the United Arab Emirates and Norway. Real dunes, sunlight and large physical environments connect costumes, dust and bodies within the same light, with visual effects extending that foundation.

Hans Zimmer’s score combines voices, rhythm and transformed timbres. Sound gives the ornithopters, sandworms and the Voice a physical impact. Listen for danger arriving before it is visible.

The film had its world premiere out of competition at Venice on September 3, 2021. The supplied Mainland rerelease materials announce November 27, 2026, promote IMAX and CINITY, and mention a Dune 3 preview. Individual theaters, editions and preview arrangements remain unannounced. The listed 155 minutes covers the feature, without adding unconfirmed bonus material.
dune-2021.language: English / Mandarin Chinese and other languages
highlights: Follow three threads first: why spice matters, why House Atreides takes Arrakis, and how the Fremen survive there.
Water makes ecology tangible: stillsuits and everyday behavior turn environmental limits into lived experience.
Observe human scale against palaces, transport ships and sandworms, especially on a large screen.
Paul’s dreams need not be read as straightforward previews; compare repeated images with events.
Listen to sandworms, ornithopters and the Voice: sound changes the viewer’s position before an explanation arrives.
Pair with Arrival and Blade Runner 2049 to compare language, architecture and fate in Villeneuve’s science fiction.
honors: 展映｜2021 78th Venice International Film Festival · Out of Competition; world premiere
获奖｜2022 94th Academy Awards · Cinematography, Film Editing, Visual Effects, Production Design, Original Score and Sound
提名｜2022 94th Academy Awards · Best Picture, Adapted Screenplay, Costume Design, and Makeup and Hairstyling
dune-2021.editorial: For viewers drawn to thoughtful science fiction, world-building and audiovisual design, or returning before the sequel. Approach it as an opening driven by politics and ecology: its contemplative pace leaves major conflicts to Part Two. Watching in order also helps resist reading Paul’s visions as an uncomplicated promise of heroic success.
warnings: Combat, blade violence and some bloody images
War, death, poison gas and sustained threat
dune-2021.contentNote: Based on UK BBFC theatrical advice and international sensory notices: combat, blade injuries, death, some bloody images, poison gas, threatening sandworms and storms, fictional hallucinogens and some language. International releases carry a flashing-image notice for photosensitive viewers. These are not Mainland Chinese classifications; specific editing or sensory differences in the 2026 rerelease remain unverified.

dune-part-two.title: Dune: Part Two
dune-part-two.bio:
Born in Quebec, Canada, in 1967, Denis Villeneuve began in French-language shorts and features. Incendies (2010) turns a family investigation toward the scars of war. Prisoners and Enemy (both 2013) explore moral uncertainty and unstable identity, while Sicario (2015) builds tension through space, rhythm and offscreen danger.

Arrival (2016) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) brought these concerns into science fiction: unfamiliar languages and monumental architecture remain connected to memory, perception and fate. His Dune films continue that interest through sound, scale and a restricted human viewpoint. Notice the pauses, distant figures and sudden threats that make a world felt before it is fully explained.
dune-part-two.syn:
After the fall of House Atreides, Paul and Jessica enter the Fremen world. Paul learns to survive in the desert, builds trust with Chani and joins resistance to Harkonnen rule. To some he is a displaced young man or a fellow fighter; to others he is the fulfillment of a prophecy.

As imperial pressure grows, belief in a messiah expands. Paul must confront the relationship between love, revenge and the future he foresees. Continuing the major events of Herbert’s first novel, Part Two is best watched after Dune: its more forceful journey also makes the idea of a hero increasingly unsettling.
dune-part-two.st:
Denis Villeneuve directed and co-wrote with Jon Spaihts. After Part One established the family, empire and spice economy, Part Two moves toward differences within Fremen society. Chani’s skepticism, Stilgar’s belief and Jessica’s actions make the creation of a public symbol central to the drama.

Returning performers include Timothée Chalamet, Zendaya, Rebecca Ferguson, Josh Brolin and Javier Bardem. Austin Butler, Florence Pugh, Christopher Walken and Léa Seydoux join the cast. Greig Fraser, Patrice Vermette and Hans Zimmer return in cinematography, production design and music.

Sandworm riding combines actors, moving equipment, dust and digital effects to give an enormous, unstable creature physical weight. Giedi Prime offers a contrasting experiment: modified digital cameras captured infrared images, producing unusual black-and-white skin and skies. This should not be confused with shooting the entire film on celluloid.

A Paris premiere at the Grand Rex took place on February 12, 2024, preceding the London event billed as the world premiere on February 15. Neither event is a festival award. The supplied materials announce a Mainland rerelease on December 4, 2026. IMAX, CINITY and Dune 3 preview arrangements depend on theater announcements; 167 minutes is the feature runtime.
highlights: Watch Part One first, then follow Paul’s movement from desert learner to public symbol.
Compare Chani and Stilgar: the same person can appear as a partner, fighter or prophecy.
Sandworm riding gives the spectacle weight through balance, footholds and sand.
Infrared black-and-white Giedi Prime contrasts with Arrakis; observe unfamiliar skin, fireworks and skies.
Within the larger action, quiet facial reactions reveal doubt, devotion and calculation.
Pair the two Dune films with Arrival to consider how foreknowledge changes choice without necessarily creating control.
honors: 获奖｜2025 97th Academy Awards · Sound and Visual Effects
提名｜2025 97th Academy Awards · Best Picture, Cinematography and Production Design
dune-part-two.editorial: For viewers who have seen Part One and want epic action intertwined with political questions. Battles and narrative movement intensify, but the most rewarding questions concern how belief mobilizes people and what a heroic image costs others. Chani’s perspective keeps the consequences beyond victory in view.
warnings: Combat, blade violence, death and bloody images
dune-part-two.contentNote: Based on UK BBFC theatrical advice: war, blade combat, death, executions, some bloody images and sustained threat, alongside fictional hallucinogens, sexual references and some language. BBFC also warns about flashing images that may affect photosensitive viewers. These are not Mainland Chinese classifications. Editing, bonus material and sensory differences in the 2026 rerelease remain unverified.

all-quiet-at-sunrise.title: All Quiet at Sunrise
all-quiet-at-sunrise.syn:
Lucy, one of the earliest known human ancestors, is often called the “grandmother of mankind.” Graduate student Ma Ke is absorbed in a linguistics thesis about her, convinced she possessed humanity’s earliest language ability. His advisor, Professor Li Tong, openly questions the argument, yet privately finds in the paper a clue that might explain her daughter’s disappearance.

As Ma Ke struggles with his writing and with reality, his mother Haiyan suddenly starts appearing in his life. She leads him to a decaying old house she has bought; within its mysteries, her secrets and wishes gradually surface, and Ma Ke’s life begins to blend with the world of his thesis. Through the murmurs of a three-million-year-old ancestor, the film asks a simple question: how do we actually say love?
all-quiet-at-sunrise.bio:
Born in Hangzhou in 1996, Zhu Xin graduated from the China Academy of Art. His debut feature Vanishing Days (2018) was selected for the Berlinale Forum and Busan’s New Currents competition and went on to more than thirty festivals, including Hong Kong, Taipei, Marrakech, Sofia and Vienna, when he was barely in his twenties. Alongside Suburban Birds and Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains, it is often discussed as part of a “Hangzhou New Wave.”

Six years later came the documentary feature A Song River (2024), which won the Youth Jury and Cinephilia Critics honors at Pingyao. All Quiet at Sunrise is his second fiction feature, which he also wrote, edited and co-produced. His films start from Hangzhou: the changing city, its dialect, family and old objects sit beside abstract questions of language, memory and time. In his director’s statement he describes the film as born of a whimsical idea and of not wanting to regret, at sixty, never making the film he wanted; he calls the script “an adventure about time,” with language as an ancient tool for glimpsing the primal energy of humans as mammals.
all-quiet-at-sunrise.st:
The story braids three strands: Ma Ke’s thesis on Lucy, Professor Li Tong’s search for her missing daughter and the old house Haiyan has bought. Yarn, camera flashes, sign language, boxes of apples and the song “Evening Bell at Nanping” become non-verbal ways of connecting, and the unspoken love between mother and son is finally bridged through these concrete things. Wang Ke plays both Ma Ke and the young Mr. Yi, while Ma Yuebo plays the old Mr. Yi and a shopkeeper; Chen Yan plays the mother Yu Haiyan, Wang Yinjie plays Li Tong, and Zhou Jiaqi makes a special appearance as Liang Xiao.

Tom Tong is chief producer, with Zhao Jin, Zhu Xin, Dia Yunzhi Wang and Wang Shimiao producing; cinematography is by Zhang Wei, production and costume design by Ding Lu, sound design by Huang Sheren and Wei Shuqian, and original music by Timon Wawreckzo. Dialogue is mostly Mandarin with some Hangzhou dialect. Produced by several Zhejiang companies including Zhejiang Tiemu Zhenying and Hangzhou Wushan Film, it is distributed by Zhejiang Times Cinema Circuit and supported by the Zhejiang Culture and Arts Development Fund.

The film had its world premiere at the 11th Berlin Critics’ Week on February 18, 2025, followed by its mainland premiere in the Beijing International Film Festival’s Filmmaker in Focus program. Wang Ke won Best Actor in HKIFF’s Young Cinema Competition (Chinese-language), and the film competed at FIRST and the Osaka Asian Film Festival, receiving a Special Mention in Osaka; its North American premiere was at Toronto’s Mulan International Film Festival. It opens in Mainland China on November 28, 2026, the same day as Zhu’s documentary A Song River. The runtime is listed as 100 minutes per Douban and the sales agent (some festival catalogues list 101).
highlights: Start with the title: “sunrise” points to the dawn before human language. Lucy in the thesis and the mother in front of Ma Ke pose the same question about a first language.
Three strands seep into one another—the thesis, the missing daughter and the old house. Notice when reality quietly turns into the world of the thesis.
Chen Yan’s mother drives the film. She rarely explains herself, yet uses yarn, apples and the old house to lead her son back to life.
Wang Ke plays both Ma Ke and the young Mr. Yi; watch how characters in two timeframes mirror each other. The role won him Best Actor in HKIFF’s Young Cinema Competition.
“Evening Bell at Nanping” recurs throughout; Hangzhou dialect, villages and old songs give an abstract linguistic story a familiar local voice.

Pair it with A Song River, opening the same day: one fiction, one documentary, both searching Hangzhou for lost sounds and a language between family members. Zhu’s debut Vanishing Days is a good follow-up.
On November 29 there is a roadshow screening at Woody Wood Cinema in Hangzhou (CINITY LED Giant Screen Hall, 19:00), with director Zhu Xin and cast members attending a post-screening Q&A.
honors: 获奖｜2025 49th Hong Kong International Film Festival · Young Cinema Competition (Chinese-language), Best Actor (Wang Ke)
提名｜2025 49th Hong Kong International Film Festival · Young Cinema Competition Firebird Award (Chinese-language)
获奖｜2025 21st Osaka Asian Film Festival · Competition, Special Mention
获奖｜Silk Road International Film Festival · Golden Silk Road Award, Best Cinematography
获奖｜2026 Dhaka International Film Festival · Audience Choice Award
提名｜2025 19th FIRST International Film Festival · Main Competition, Best Feature Film
展映｜2025 11th Berlin Critics’ Week · World premiere
展映｜2025 15th Beijing International Film Festival · Beijing Film Panorama (Filmmaker in Focus)
展映｜2025 Hainan Island International Film Festival · Panorama
展映｜2025 Mulan International Film Festival, Toronto · North American premiere
all-quiet-at-sunrise.editorial: For viewers who enjoy conceptual cinema and are willing to be caught off guard by everyday emotion. The film sets the deep-time imagination of anthropology and linguistics beside an old house in Hangzhou and a mother. Its structure jumps and deliberately blurs fantasy and reality, so a first viewing may take patience, but what lands is the love between mother and son that neither can put into words, and many viewers have been moved by the ending. If you prefer linear storytelling, try watching it as a prose poem about time and family.
warnings: A missing family member and the search for her
Emotional strain from family secrets and generational conflict
all-quiet-at-sunrise.contentNote: Checked against the official synopsis and festival materials: the story involves a professor’s missing daughter, distance between mother and son and family secrets across two generations, with a melancholy tone. No official classification or scene-by-scene review of the mainland release has been obtained, and sensory elements such as flashing images or sudden loud sounds remain unverified. These topic notes are not an official rating.

a-song-river.title: A Song River
a-song-river.syn:
Feeling powerless in his present life, Zhu Xin wants to find the Hangzhou of the past. Across the river from his home lies Phoenix Mountain, where an entrance seems to open: a thousand years ago Su Shi wrote the ci poem “Jiangchengzi” there. Ci were once songs, and the rhythm between the lines sounds like a call from home.

With Hong Kong lyricist Siu Hak, he sets out to trace the poem’s original pronunciation and melody. Confronted with the gaps in history, the plan drifts off course, and the idea of “home” in both men’s minds quietly changes shape. More than a documentary, the film is a dramatized reconstruction of its maker and of the blanks in history.
a-song-river.bio:
Born in Hangzhou in 1996, Zhu Xin graduated from the China Academy of Art and began making films as a teenager. His debut fiction feature Vanishing Days (2018) was selected for the Berlinale Forum and Busan’s New Currents competition and screened at more than thirty festivals, placing him in discussions of a “Hangzhou New Wave.”

A Song River, his first feature in six years and his first documentary feature, won the Youth Jury and Cinephilia Critics honors after premiering at Pingyao. He then completed his second fiction feature, All Quiet at Sunrise, which premiered at Berlin Critics’ Week in 2025. Both films start from Hangzhou—one through documentary, one through fiction—to ask about the distance between language, home and family. They open in Mainland China on the same day, November 28, 2026.
a-song-river.st:
The film grew from Zhu Xin’s fascination with Cantonese lyrics. Some argue that Cantonese preserves more of the sounds of older Chinese, so he invited Hong Kong lyricist and cartoonist Siu Hak, writer of well-known Cantopop lyrics, to help reconstruct the reading and melody of Su Shi’s “Jiangchengzi: On the Lake, Written with Zhang Xian.” The plan to shoot in Hong Kong collapsed under 2022 travel restrictions; “stuck in Hangzhou,” the crew let Hangzhou and Hong Kong meet on screen, and the failed attempt became part of the film.

Zhu has said the project began as a more academic essay documentary before he reshot it around the links between Song ci, Hong Kong pop and Cantonese. Straight documentary passages alternate with deliberately staged scenes, using different cameras and aspect ratios, and arguments within the crew and with his mother remain in the cut. Music historian Zheng Zuxiang and scholars Lu Beirong, Xi Xunqiang and Zheng Zining appear to discuss the sounds of Song ci; the director’s mother Guo Weimin is billed as a lead, with special appearances by Wu Wei and Wang Wanshui. In the end Zhu finds the old Hangzhou in his parents’ wedding videotape.

Locations include Phoenix Mountain, West Lake through the seasons and Lingyin. Produced by Hangzhou Wushan Film with producers Li Zheng and Wang Lili, written by Zhu Xin, Shen Zhen, Wang Lili and Chen Xinjialan, with sound effects by Huang Sheren, it was selected for the China Federation of Literary and Art Circles’ young creators’ support program. It premiered in Pingyao’s Hidden Dragons section on September 27, 2024, then screened at the West Lake International Documentary Festival, the Golden Rooster showcase, HKIFF and the Beijing International Film Festival. The runtime is listed as 97 minutes per Douban (the West Lake festival listed 95).
highlights: Read Su Shi’s “Jiangchengzi: On the Lake, Written with Zhang Xian” first, then watch the film treat a Song poem as a song whose voice must be found.
Documentary and staging intertwine. Rather than sorting what is real, watch how the director turns the failed plan into the subject.
Hangzhou and Hong Kong mirror each other: Siu Hak’s Cantonese lyrics and the home Su Shi wrote about after leaving it share the same homesickness.
Arguments with his mother and his parents’ wedding videotape bring a documentary about Song poetry back to one family.
West Lake through the seasons, Phoenix Mountain and Lingyin invite viewers who know Hangzhou to compare the city on screen with the one in memory.
Pair it with All Quiet at Sunrise, opening the same day: the same director uses documentary and fiction to ask how language and love get spoken.
On November 29 there is a roadshow screening at Woody Wood Cinema in Hangzhou (CINITY LED Giant Screen Hall, 15:30), with director Zhu Xin and cast members attending a post-screening Q&A.
honors: 获奖｜2024 8th Pingyao International Film Festival · Youth Jury Award (New Generation China)
获奖｜2024 8th Pingyao International Film Festival · Cinephilia Critics’ Award
入围｜2024 8th Pingyao International Film Festival · Hidden Dragons
展映｜2024 7th West Lake International Documentary Festival · Chinese-language Focus
展映｜2024 Glory of Documentary

a-song-river.editorial: For viewers interested in Song poetry, Cantopop and the memory of Hangzhou, who can accept a documentary without a definitive answer. This is not an explainer on classical verse but a search that changes course midway; its real subject is a young man disoriented by a changing city, rebuilding his connection to his mother and his hometown. Reactions are divided: those expecting picturesque West Lake scenery or rigorous scholarship may be disappointed, while viewers willing to join the director’s “futile” search may find unexpected warmth at the end.

24-flavors.title: 24 Flavors
24-flavors.syn:
Returning to Guangzhou from Britain, April discovers that her long-separated parents have reunited. Her mother Qiaozhen’s herbal-tea shop faces demolition, while her father Yongtang has re-entered her life. April had planned to take her mother abroad; instead, she must revisit the family history she has tried to leave behind.

A father’s betrayal, a mother’s decisions and the wounds April carries from growing up make reunion difficult. Each holds a different memory of the family. Around a neighborhood tea shop, the film explores bitterness that cannot easily be swallowed and care that is difficult to express.
24-flavors.bio:
Chinese writer-director Elaine Huang makes her fiction-feature debut with 24 Flavors. She studied directing at the Central Academy of Drama, continued at Goldsmiths, University of London, and undertook visiting study at New York University. Her earlier work spans theater and shorts, including Kuipeng, Little White Whale and Blindness. This cross-disciplinary background brings an interest in performance, relationships and everyday detail.

In interviews, Huang traces the film’s beginnings to a cousin’s family experience. Rather than deciding who is right, she asks why people of different generations make choices that others find difficult to accept. Years of project development and financing led to a debut rooted in Guangzhou and women’s experiences within a family.
24-flavors.st:
The title refers to a bitter Guangdong herbal tea blended from many ingredients. The shop joins family life to urban change: for the mother it is both a livelihood and a place with a history. Its threatened demolition coincides with the family’s reunion, without making reconciliation a simple answer.

Sylvia Chang plays Qiaozhen, Kenny Bee plays Yongtang and Angela Yuen plays their daughter April. Chang and Bee reunite on screen after many years, while Yuen provides a returning daughter’s observation and resistance. Watch pauses, looks and the distance between bodies when all three share a scene.

Supported by Guangdong’s young-film-talent program and Guangzhou film-industry funding, the project passed through the 2018 Wu Tianming pitch event, the 2020 Golden Rooster main project selection and the 2023 Golden Rooster works-in-progress selection. These are development selections and support, not interchangeable film awards. Shot in Guangzhou’s old neighborhoods, the production involves executive producer Ng Kwan-cheung, artistic director Liao Ching-song and producer Ding Yu, with production designer Poon Yik-sum and sound director Tu Duu-chih.

The film screened in Xiamen’s Golden Rooster Chinese-language showcase in November 2024, SIFF’s Chinese New Style program in 2025, and HIFF’s Spotlight on Hong Kong. Its 2025 Cannes Marché du Film presentation belonged to a Chinese young-filmmaker promotion program, not Cannes official competition. The supplied release materials announce November 27, 2026, in Mainland China. This screening is listed as the 127-minute full version (earlier catalogue runtime: 107 minutes; HIFF listed 106 minutes).
highlights: Enter Guangzhou through the tea shop: streets and demolition connect urban change to private relationships.
Try each family member’s viewpoint; the same choice carries different weight for the daughter, mother and father.
Chang and Bee’s renewed collaboration makes familiarity and distance equally useful things to observe.
April wants to protect her mother; consider when protection might cross another person’s boundaries.
Bitterness is an entry point, not necessarily an instruction to forgive. Notice which wounds remain unresolved.
Pair with Sylvia Chang’s Love Education and Ann Hui’s The Way We Are to compare care, generational distance and everyday spaces.

hideaway-the-dossiers.title: Hideaway: The Dossiers
hideaway-the-dossiers.syn:
Shanghai, 1942. A collection of secret documents is hidden inside a shikumen residence. Underground workers Xu Shuting and Shen Yulin pose as an ordinary married couple, protecting the archives while keeping up the routines of renting a home, preparing meals and speaking to neighbours.

Surveillance and searches turn everyday exchanges into tests of identity and trust. The film draws on the history of the Central Archives, concentrating a long collective undertaking into the precarious domestic life of two people.
hideaway-the-dossiers.bio:
Shanghai filmmaker Zheng Dasheng works across fiction, documentary and filmed opera. His films include The Death of Wang Bo, The Antique, Useless Man, Bangzi Melody and the Peking-opera film The Upright Official Yu Chenglong; he also worked on 1921.

His interest in history often takes shape through ordinary bodies, routines and social spaces. In Hideaway: The Dossiers, watch how a courtyard, its doors and its shared corridors become a map of what the characters can say and do.
hideaway-the-dossiers.st:
Produced by Shanghai Film Group, the film draws on the history of successive guardians of the Central Archives. Rather than surveying the entire period chronologically, it concentrates on occupied Shanghai and a couple whose daily identities conceal a dangerous responsibility.

Zheng has described several rounds of script development and research into urban, everyday and oral history. Domestic space is integral to the drama: a room, a route through a corridor or a sound from next door can change the meaning of an otherwise ordinary exchange. Yuan Hong and Li Yanxi lead an ensemble including Shao Feng, Xie Chengying and Li Xiaochuan.

The supplied Star Screenings timetable specifies 132 minutes. The 21 November screening starts at 14:30 in Hall 3 of Huaying Xingkong Cinema, followed by an approximately 30-minute discussion with Zheng Dasheng and Shao Feng.
hideaway-the-dossiers.editorial: For viewers interested in historical drama, ensemble acting and the use of domestic space. Watch how the effort to appear ordinary changes the characters' smallest gestures. The discussion offers an opportunity to ask how historical research, invented characters and genre expectations were balanced.
highlights: Follow doors, shared rooms and routes through the courtyard as a map of information.
Compare characters' public behaviour with their private exchanges.
Watch the ensemble without rushing to sort everyone into fixed categories.
Ask the director and actor how tension was built through routine actions.

never-too-late-2024.title: Never Too Late
never-too-late-2024.syn:
At eighty, Deng Guiying decides to divorce Yang Qiaoyuan after sixty years of marriage. Their granddaughter Yang Lizhu begins filming, asking what lies behind a decision that has startled the family and their small-town community.

Separation does not end the visits, arguments, meals and concern. Listening to each grandparent, Yang gradually discovers individual wishes and disappointments concealed inside a familiar family story, as illness, ageing and loss alter the conversation.
never-too-late-2024.bio:
Born in Hunan, Yang Lizhu graduated from Beijing Film Academy in 2016, specialising in photography, and participated in a documentary workshop exchange with Shih Hsin University in Taiwan. Never Too Late is her first feature documentary.

She is both filmmaker and granddaughter. Her voice and relationship to the people on screen are part of the film, which moves from recording surprising family news towards listening to two entire lives.
never-too-late-2024.st:
The project began with the grandmother's unexpected divorce and developed from student-era images into a feature. Producer Zheng Quan joined the project; editors Yu Xiaochuan and Du Mengwei helped shape years of family material into a sustained narrative.

Instead of treating divorce only as a newsworthy event, the film connects the grandparents' daily habits to their memories of education, work and marriage. Its family perspective allows intimacy while also raising questions about what a camera can and cannot understand.

The film had its world premiere in the 2024 Doc@PÖFF Competition and subsequently screened at Hainan and other festivals. Competition selection, a jury special mention and later recommendations are recorded separately.

The supplied local timetable uses a Chinese title variant ending in an additional er; it is the same film. This 81-minute screening starts at 19:00 on 22 November in Hall 1 of SFC Jiaxing Babaiban LUXE, followed by an approximately 30-minute discussion with producer Zheng Quan.
never-too-late-2024.editorial: For viewers interested in family images, intergenerational conversations and intimate relationships. Listen to both grandparents as individuals and notice the humour beside the silences. The discussion with the producer can explore how a family short developed into a feature. Those recently affected by illness or bereavement may wish to read the content notes first.
highlights: Listen to each grandparent's wishes without reducing either person to a position in an argument.
Notice the everyday ties that continue after divorce.
Pay attention to the granddaughter's voice and the camera's closeness.
Ask the producer about editing, development and bringing a family film to audiences.

red-river-2009.title: Red River
red-river-2009.syn:
On the China–Vietnam border, the consequences of war remain present in ordinary lives. A Tao, affected by childhood trauma after losing her father, comes to China to stay with her aunt. In a small border town she meets A Xia, who runs a street karaoke stall, and attaches memories of her father to him.

Her singing brings the two closer, but also draws them into other people's desires and struggles for control. Against the river and the surrounding town, the film follows a relationship shaped by care, dependency and dangers neither can easily escape.
red-river-2009.bio:
Chinese director and screenwriter Zhang Jiarui has often explored regional life and personal relationships. When Ruoma Was Seventeen, Huayao Bride in Shangrila and Red River are commonly described as his Yunnan trilogy.

In Red River, landscape is both a source of visual lyricism and a practical condition of movement, encounter and escape. The film extends his interest in individuals and place towards the lasting consequences of war.
red-river-2009.st:
Inspired by an oral account from a Vietnamese woman, the film developed into a drama about the aftermath of war and life along a border. Zhang Jingchu plays A Tao, Nick Cheung plays A Xia, and Loletta Lee and Danny Lee form part of the world surrounding their relationship.

Production took place in China and Vietnam with a multinational crew. Zhang has discussed the difficulty of communicating across languages and the practical work needed to establish a shared understanding on set. Voices, music and everyday routines contribute to the film's sense of place.

A global-premiere event was held in Kunming in April 2009 before the mainland release. Zhang won Best Director at the 16th Beijing College Student Film Festival, where Zhang Jingchu was named the most popular actress. These historical records are separate from this 2026 screening.

The supplied Star Screenings timetable specifies 103 minutes; other release records list different lengths. This screening starts at 18:30 on 24 November in the TCL Auditorium at Jiaxing University, followed by an approximately 30-minute discussion with Zhang Jiarui and guest Li Xiangmo.
red-river-2009.editorial: For viewers interested in border narratives, performance and the emotional style of 2000s Chinese cinema. Alongside its tragic romance, consider questions of care, coercion and how much agency the story gives A Tao. These specific choices offer useful subjects for the discussion with the director.
highlights: Notice how war survives through memory, bodies and relationships.
Compare what A Tao, A Xia and the surrounding characters think their relationship means.
Follow the interaction between the river landscape, singing and street life.
Discuss performance and the relationship between heightened emotion and character agency.

wtm26-ai-and-you.title: AI Means Love
wtm26-ai-and-you.syn:
The protagonist goes viral with a video of an "AI grandma". At his grandmother's grave he meets his father for the first time in six years, and sees how moved his father is by the AI grandma.

He decides to build a better AI grandma as a gift for his father, hoping to mend a father-son relationship that is inverted, out of joint and full of contradictions. The technical problems prove far harder than expected, and years of resentment, clashing outlooks and very different ways of living complicate the plan further.
wtm26-ai-and-you.editorial: For viewers curious about how AI enters family feeling. More than a film about technology, it is an attempt to get closer to a father through a digital relative; watch for what father and son cannot say on camera.
highlights: An AI grandma links the memories and distances of three generations.
Technical hurdles and family wounds unfold together, without a predetermined ending.

wtm26-ai-and-you.bio: Qian Yicheng directed the documentary AI Means Love. His earlier work includes the short Someone Is Singing. He began exploring generative AI and moving images in 2023, and started following this film's central family in March 2024.
wtm26-ai-and-you.st:
Also presented under the Chinese title 爱（AI）和你之间, the documentary follows Hu Renliang and his father Hu Yanlin. The viral “AI Grandma” video from 2023 provides its starting point. The director then follows their attempt to build a digital grandmother, placing technical obstacles alongside everyday family life.

Qian focuses on the father and son's relationship. Recreating a familiar face and voice cannot conduct a face-to-face conversation for them; the film asks how the living can come to know one another again.

wtm26-tiger-tonight.title: The Angry People
wtm26-tiger-tonight.editorial: For viewers who like dark comedy and ensembles of ordinary people. Behind a night of absurd brawling lies the price-war pressure on freight drivers; the laughter leaves the weight of life at the bottom.
honors: Screening｜2026 Wu Tianming Young Film Festival · Industry Screenings: Beyond the First Feature (closed screening)
wtm26-tiger-tonight.contentNote: Based on the official synopsis: arguments, fighting and property damage among truck drivers, in a dark-comedy tone. Not reviewed shot by shot; intensity, flashing and sudden loud sounds are unverified. This is not an official rating.
wtm26-tiger-tonight.syn: Shen Can, a young truck driver, takes jobs at low prices and upsets the freight market. Middle-aged driver Ma Dehu only wants to warn him off, but the talk goes badly, Ma loses control, hits Shen and smashes his windscreen. Humiliated and furious, Shen decides to hit back, and the two have an absurd, fierce fight that lasts the night. By dawn the storm has passed and they make peace, only to see other drivers brawling over cheap cargo. Watching them, the two finally resolve to face together the chaos of cut-throat competition and survival at the bottom of the industry.
wtm26-tiger-tonight.st:
Supervising producer Zhou Youchao; producers A Xin and Yue Yichen; written and directed by Deng Xinyangyi.

The cast includes Chu Buhua Jie, Bai Nannan, Cai Yunhong, Hu Junshuang and Gao Yan. The younger and older drivers work within the same freight economy: their clash grows from temperament as well as the pressure to underbid. Reconciliation at dawn does not remove that shared predicament.

The project was presented at a Shaanxi young filmmakers' showcase in 2026.
highlights: A quarrel escalates into an absurd all-night fight, and by dawn the two make peace.
The price war among freight drivers told as dark-comedy ensemble drama.

wtm26-nine-piece-band.syn:
As summer draws to an end, a nine-member band about to split up takes one last job: holding a funeral for a small purple flower. The request is baffling and the road is long, but the band decides to see it through.

After the funeral, the members find that this journey of farewell and healing is not quite over.
wtm26-nine-piece-band.st:
According to the China Film Administration's project registration, the film was registered in Fujian in 2025 by Wucaigong (Xiamen) Film & Culture Co., with Sun Xiangyu as screenwriter.

Shot on 16mm film, the cast includes Quanzhou Hongsheng Band, Cai Xueqing, Bao Dongdong, Wu Xinran and Ke Qingxiang. A funeral for a small flower connects the band's final journey; music, travel and ritual offer ways to express loss and reconnect.
wtm26-nine-piece-band.editorial: For viewers who enjoy slightly absurd road and ensemble stories. A funeral for a flower is the excuse to set out; what is really being sent off may be the band itself, and the summer.
highlights: A band's last job before splitting becomes a farewell journey.
Nine members on the road, loosening up and making peace.

wtm26-hoh-xil-and-me.title: A Woman in Their Eyes
wtm26-hoh-xil-and-me.syn: After injury ends her career, national paragliding champion Gu Ying heads into the uninhabited Hoh Xil to film wildlife. Over ten years on the plateau she records conflict and coexistence between people and animals on a beautiful, harsh land, and gradually becomes part of it herself.
wtm26-hoh-xil-and-me.bio:
Gu Ying was a national women's paragliding champion before turning to wildlife photography. The turning point came at the Shenzhen Bay wetlands, when a borrowed camera caught a black-faced spoonbill taking off and she felt she had flown back into the sky. She has since photographed over a thousand bird species across seven continents, with work included in the Handbook of the Birds of the World.

A Woman in Their Eyes condenses her ten years in the wilderness into a feature documentary. She also co-produced the nature documentary series on the Three-River-Source region.
wtm26-hoh-xil-and-me.st:
Shot over a decade with about 10,000 hours of footage, most of it filmed by Gu herself, the film keeps even the whispers behind the camera. She wants audiences to feel as if hiding in the tent with her.

The Tibetan antelope migration is the through line: in 2016 she filmed antelopes refusing to pass under a railway bridge; seven years later the herd walks under it alongside passing trains. Her method was to wait: into a hide at 5:30 a.m., there all day, letting the animals come close only when they trusted her.

In 2025 the film was selected for the From Shanxi section of the 9th Pingyao International Film Festival. Gu later said she was still refining the cut, trying to play down herself so animals and rangers take centre stage.

Gu Ying directs and photographs the film, producing with Zhang Huiting under supervising producer Lei Jianjun. Alongside migration, it preserves the filmmaker's waiting, learning and adaptation, following both her changing relationship with Hoh Xil and the animals' encounters with human activity.
wtm26-hoh-xil-and-me.editorial: For viewers who like nature documentaries and accept raw, unpolished images. Not a glossy landscape film, but the record of one person placing herself in the wilderness for ten years.
highlights: Ten years of filming and about 10,000 hours of footage, mostly shot by the director.
The antelope migration charts seven years of change at a railway bridge.
From intruder to participant: the director steps back so animals and rangers lead.

wtm26-migration.syn:
Set on the grasslands of Abag Banner in Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia, a story of a bond and a reconciliation spanning twenty years.

Two elderly women from the grassland, estranged by a misunderstanding years earlier, set out with an old horse. Travelling together and revisiting the past, they approach each other again and face what remains unresolved.
wtm26-migration.bio: Ajijiya is a young director at Xi'an Film Studio; he wrote and directed this film.
wtm26-migration.st:
Produced first by Xi'an Film Studio and co-made with the publicity departments of Shaanxi and Inner Mongolia, the film began shooting in Abag Banner on 7 May 2026. Golden Rooster best actress winners Badema and Naren Hua lead the cast; Golden Rooster–winning children's film director Bai Zhiqiang and screenwriter Yuan Yuan are supervising producers.

According to the launch report, the film explores ethnic culture, women's strength and the value of life through life on the grassland.

The screenplay was presented in Xi'an Film Studio's Xinghe creative screenplay programme under the writer credit Shi Xiaoyu (Ajijiya). The two women and an old horse turn the grassland into a journey through memory, care and reconciliation.
wtm26-migration.editorial: For viewers drawn to grassland stories and strong female performances; watch how the relationship shifts across twenty years.
highlights: Golden Rooster best actress winners Badema and Naren Hua together.
Shot on location in Abag Banner across a twenty-year story.

wtm26-west-chamber.title: The Romance of the Western Chamber
wtm26-west-chamber.syn:
Scholar Zhang Junrui meets Cui Yingying, daughter of a chancellor's family, at Pujiu Temple, and the two fall for each other. When rebel general Sun Feihu besieges the temple to seize Yingying, her mother promises her hand to whoever drives the soldiers off. Zhang lifts the siege, but the mother breaks her word.

The maid Hongniang works cleverly between the lovers, while Yingying wrestles with feeling, propriety and reason. Adapted from Yuan Zhen's Tang tale Yingying's Story, with material from Wang Shifu's Romance of the Western Chamber.
wtm26-west-chamber.bio: Cui Xiaodong worked on Hou Hsiao-hsien's The Assassin and has long focused on art-house filmmaking; this Kunqu opera film is his work as director. At the Shanghai post-screening talk he said he had looked at Yue Feng's Shaw Brothers version, but could not build a complete garden and temple as they had, and had to find a way to tell the story and a style of his own in limited space.
wtm26-west-chamber.st:
Led by Jiangsu Film Group, the film shot in Kunshan from 20 June to 22 July 2025, rebuilding traditional architecture 1:1 with Xiangshan-school craft. Mei Feng contributed to the screenplay and Suzhou Kunqu Opera Theatre writer Wanzhou wrote the opera libretto, combining the Tang tale and Wang Shifu's play.

The Suzhou Kunqu Opera Theatre supported the production throughout, with Wang Fang and Zhang Jun as Kunqu artistic advisers. Art director Hwarng Wern-ying and cinematographer Yao Hung-i from Taiwan shaped the look. Wu Yuheng and Zhang Chuwen play Zhang Junrui and Yingying; Kunqu performer Wang Anan plays Hongniang.

The film had its world premiere on 15 June 2026 at SHO Shanghai Film Art Centre in the Special Screenings section of the 28th Shanghai International Film Festival.

Kong Jinlei worked on editing and guzheng musician Chang Jing composed the score. Garden architecture, performers' movement and Kunqu singing work together to tell the classical love story through space, sound and performance.
wtm26-west-chamber.editorial: For viewers who love classical aesthetics, opera and garden imagery, and for first-timers to Kunqu. Watch how the film rebuilds the Western Chamber in limited space and joins arias to screen storytelling.
highlights: Art director Hwarng Wern-ying and cinematographer Yao Hung-i of The Assassin.
Full support from the Suzhou Kunqu Opera Theatre, with Wang Fang and Zhang Jun advising.
A new adaptation combining Yingying's Story and Wang Shifu's play.

wtm26-goodbye-furkid.title: Goodbye, Furkid
wtm26-goodbye-furkid.syn: Dongting, at a low point in life, ends up with a few other losers: a father with a criminal record, a mother who has lost a child and a young driver in debt. These overlooked people drift together and run a pet funeral home. On the ruins of their lives, by helping others send off their pets, they lay their own broken pasts to rest and form a family without blood ties, supporting one another as they look for a glimmer of light.

Producer Xu Weiliang; written by Zhang Yizhe and Li Yixuan.

Starring Peng Jing, Liang Ji, Sun Jiawen and Xia Bing. The pet funeral home connects strangers who must support grieving owners while finding room for their own losses and failures. Everyday care and a gradually formed family without blood ties provide the emotional focus.

On the ruins of their lives, a family without blood ties looks for light.

wtm26-west-border.title: West Border
wtm26-west-border.syn:
A motorcycle pulled from a border river sets off two murders and draws two groups of strangers into a journey back and forth between two county towns on China's south-western border.

Amid rumours of the end of the world, a father searching for his daughter and a policeman searching for himself keep moving, an uncertain father-daughter bond takes shape, and truth and illusion grow harder to tell apart.
wtm26-west-border.bio: Luo Yan graduated from the Department of Dramatic Literature at the Central Academy of Drama and comes from Hengyang, Hunan. She was planner and executive producer on The Looming Storm, winner of the Best Artistic Contribution Award at the 30th Tokyo International Film Festival. West Border, which she wrote and directed, is her first feature.
wtm26-west-border.st:
Originally titled 1999, the screenplay was selected by the Wu Tianming Young Directors Special Fund and won its Best Young Director Film Project Award. Li Yu and Fang Li are supervising producers, Duan Yihong is artistic adviser, Zhao Longlong shot the film and Korean editor Hahm Sung-won co-edited.

Luo calls it a fantasy grounded in a realist story: road movie and murder case, the detective and femme fatale of film noir, and a wish to bring Latin American literature's political metaphors and cult and B-movie aesthetics to south-west China. She deliberately left her hometown to shoot on the overgrown Yunnan border, and wrote her complicated feelings about her father into the possible father-daughter thread.

The film premiered in the Hidden Dragons section of the 9th Pingyao International Film Festival in 2025 and then screened at the 7th Hainan Island International Film Festival; in 2026 it was selected for Festival Allers-Retours and, out of competition, the Milano Film Fest.

Internationally presented as West Border, the film is also listed on some platforms as Western Border or by its earlier title, 1999. These refer to Luo Yan's film with Pan Binlong and Chloe Maayan. A border river, a motorcycle and an uncertain father-daughter bond connect its two groups of characters.
wtm26-west-border.editorial: For viewers who like genre blends, border road movies and fantasy moods. Don't watch it only as a whodunit: the end-of-the-world rumours, humid jungle and ambiguous father-daughter bond are what it really builds.
highlights: Developed as 1999 with support from the Wu Tianming fund, now back at the Wu Tianming festival.
Produced under Li Yu and Fang Li; starring Pan Binlong and Chloe Maayan.
Film noir, road movie and fantasy meet on the south-western border.

triangle-of-sadness.title: Triangle of Sadness
triangle-of-sadness.syn:
Model couple Carl and Yaya are invited onto a luxury yacht to holiday with wealthy passengers. Disaster strikes at sea and the survivors are stranded on a desert island, where the cleaner who has survival skills becomes the one everyone relies on, and the old order of wealth and power is turned upside down.

The story starts with an argument over who should pay for dinner. On the yacht, modelling and social media buy the couple a free trip, while the crew is trained to grant guests their every wish. A storm hits during the captain’s dinner. Once ashore, cleaner Abigail can feed the group, and for the first time she gets to decide who eats.
triangle-of-sadness.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
triangle-of-sadness.st:
In developing the film, Östlund drew on his fashion-photographer wife’s knowledge of modelling and brand marketing. On the yacht and island he puts the same characters under two systems of labour: one organised around serving the rich and the other around the skills needed to survive.

Triangle of Sadness is Ruben Östlund’s first English-language feature. The title borrows a fashion-industry term for the area of wrinkles between the eyebrows. Östlund announced the project after The Square won the Palme d’Or, describing a wild satire of fashion and the super-rich built on “appearance as capital” and “beauty as currency”.

Shot by Fredrik Wenzel, the film premiered in competition at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in May 2022 and won the Palme d’Or, making Östlund one of the few directors to win it twice. It went on to win Best Film at the European Film Awards, received three Academy Award nominations (Best Picture, Director and Original Screenplay) and took six Guldbagge Awards in Sweden, including Best Film and Best Director.
highlights: Notice the instructions at the model casting. A smile means something different at each price point, and the scene shows how quickly the industry assigns value to a body.
At the captain’s dinner, etiquette, the weather and the political slogans on the loudspeaker pull the scene apart. Listen first, then watch how long the guests maintain their composure.
