triangle-of-sadness.editorial: Watch three acts of distribution across the film: the restaurant bill, the demands placed on the yacht crew, and the food handed out on the island. The value of beauty, money and labour shifts with each setting. Dolly de Leon makes Abigail’s move from serving others to setting the rules especially vivid.

the-square-2017.title: The Square
the-square-2017.syn:
The chief curator of a prestigious Stockholm museum, trying to stage a controversial new exhibition, falls into a crisis that is both professional and personal.

Curator Christian is preparing an installation called The Square, which asks visitors to step inside a marked area and practise mutual trust and care. Then his phone and wallet are stolen, prompting a rash attempt to recover them, and the museum’s publicity team makes a provocative video for the exhibition. Christian must deal with the people affected by his choices as well as an institution trying to contain the fallout.
the-square-2017.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
the-square-2017.st:
The installation had a real-world prototype. Östlund and longtime collaborator Kalle Boman exhibited a square at the Vandalorum museum in Värnamo, Sweden, for visitors to test an agreement to look after one another. The film places that work in a fictional Stockholm museum and tests the agreement through publicity, fundraising and daily life.

The film premiered in competition at the 70th Cannes Film Festival in May 2017 and won the Palme d’Or. Claes Bang plays museum curator Christian, alongside Elisabeth Moss, Dominic West and motion-capture performer Terry Notary.

At that year’s European Film Awards The Square won six prizes, including European Film, Director and Actor. It was also Sweden’s Oscar nominee for Best Foreign Language Film and received a Golden Globe nomination in the same category.
highlights: Both the street theft and the installation begin with an appeal between strangers. Notice whom Christian trusts in each setting.
Terry Notary’s dinner performance leaves the guests in the frame. The tension builds as everyone watches and nobody knows when to speak.

the-square-2017.editorial: Look at who gets to define the situation in the opening interview, the publicity meeting and the donors’ dinner. The museum can write a graceful statement about trust. The film keeps asking how its staff behave when someone actually needs their help.

force-majeure-2014.title: Force Majeure
force-majeure-2014.syn:
A Swedish family travels to the French Alps for a few days of skiing. The sun is shining and the slopes are spectacular, but during lunch at a mountainside restaurant an avalanche turns everything upside down. Diners scatter; the mother, Ebba, tries to shield the children while calling for her husband, Tomas — who has fled on his own to save himself. When reality returns, the expected disaster never happens, leaving only awkward laughter, yet the family’s world has been shaken to its core.

Tomas’s unexpected act forces them to re-examine their roles and assumptions, above all the image of the father, which now carries a huge question mark. As the holiday nears its end, Tomas and Ebba’s marriage hangs in the balance while Tomas struggles desperately to win back his dignity as head of the family.

Force Majeure is an observational comedy that dissects the male role in modern family life.

The holiday goes on: the family still has to ski, eat and come and go together. When Ebba tells friends what happened, Tomas gives a different account. The argument spreads beyond the couple and leaves everyone at the table wondering how they would have acted.
force-majeure-2014.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
force-majeure-2014.st:
Östlund had made skiing films before turning the mountains into a setting for studying people. The production used locations in the French Alps, British Columbia and a Swedish resort. In his first collaboration with cinematographer Fredrik Wenzel, a fixed frame could hold both the vast slope and a family deciding how to react.

The English release title, Force Majeure, comes from the contract clause for unforeseeable events; the Swedish title Turist means “tourist”. Shot by Fredrik Wenzel and edited by Jacob Secher Schulsinger, the film was selected for Un Certain Regard at the 67th Cannes Film Festival in 2014, where it won the Jury Prize, and then screened in Toronto’s Special Presentations.

It received a Golden Globe nomination for Best Foreign Language Film and won six Guldbagge Awards in 2015: Best Film, Director, Cinematography, Screenplay, Editing and Supporting Actor. Hollywood remade it in 2020 as Downhill.
highlights: The avalanche approaches in a wide shot. Watch the instant the diners stop filming with their phones and start leaving their seats.
Ski equipment, resort routines and the recurring Vivaldi make the holiday feel choreographed. The comedy comes out when someone falls out of step.

force-majeure-2014.editorial: Follow the tables where Ebba recounts the avalanche. First she experiences it, then she has to persuade others that she saw what she saw. Tomas’s corrections and the friends’ attempts to keep the peace give the film its sharpest moments long after the snow clears.

play-2011.title: Play
play-2011.syn:
Play is a social observation based on real bullying cases. In central Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2006 and 2008, a group of boys aged 12 to 14 robbed other children around 40 times. The young robbers used an elaborate con known as the “little brother number” — relying on sophisticated role-play and gang rhetoric rather than physical violence.

The film compresses a series of cases into a single day. A group approaches three boys at a shopping centre and asks one to prove that his phone is his. Eager to clear things up, the boys follow them through a city busy with passengers and pedestrians. With every new version of the story, it becomes harder for them to leave.
play-2011.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
play-2011.st:
Östlund consulted court documents and spoke with people involved before turning the incidents into fiction, letting the actors sustain the rhythm of hesitation, negotiation and waiting. The Swedish release provoked debate over race, the portrayal of minority youths and when adults should intervene. Directors’ Fortnight places the film within his continuing exploration of the effects of groups on individuals.

The film draws on a real series of cases in Gothenburg between 2006 and 2008. Östlund cast eight non-professional boys and filmed them in a series of wide long takes to heighten the feeling of real time.

Play premiered in the Directors’ Fortnight at Cannes in 2011, winning the Coup de cœur prize, then won Best Director at Tokyo, Guldbagge Awards for Best Director and Cinematography, and the 2012 Nordic Council Film Prize. Its release sparked fierce debate in the Swedish press.
highlights: The long takes let each awkward exchange play out. People at the edge of the frame can hear the words without necessarily knowing what they are doing.
The shopping centre and public transport carry on as usual. Pair the film with Incident by a Bank to compare the ways Östlund places bystanders inside an unfolding event.

play-2011.editorial: Listen for every reasonable-sounding request for one more explanation. The boys’ wish to clear up a misunderstanding is what keeps them going. The wide frames also leave time to consider what the passengers and other adults around them may have noticed.

incident-by-a-bank.title: Incident by a Bank
incident-by-a-bank.syn:
In detailed, humorous real time, the film records a failed bank robbery and keenly observes how people react to the unexpected. Shot in a single take with more than 96 people in precise choreography, it recreates an event that really happened in 2006.

People are passing the bank as usual. Two witnesses slowly realise the commotion may be a robbery. Some pedestrians stop and others keep walking, while fragments of talk keep drawing the witnesses’ attention elsewhere. A story that could fit in a headline takes as long as it took the people there to recognise it.
incident-by-a-bank.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
incident-by-a-bank.st:
The short turns witnessed confusion into a carefully rehearsed event. A wide source image leaves room to reframe the continuous action in post-production. Cinematographer Måns Diwad and Östlund, who also edited the film, use this technique to direct our attention while life elsewhere in the frame keeps moving.

The film recreates an attempted robbery that Östlund and producer Erik Hemmendorff witnessed in Stockholm in June 2006. It is a single take in which 96 performers move to a precise choreography; the camera movement was generated by computer in post-production.

It won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 2010 Berlinale, along with the Grand Prix and Audience Award at Tampere and Best European Short at Cork.
highlights: Listen to the two witnesses. They start inventing explanations for what they see before they are sure what is happening.
Watch the pedestrians at the edges. The robbery and the ordinary life of the street share the same stretch of time.

incident-by-a-bank.editorial: Try it as a game of following people. The frame leads you towards a suspicious movement and you may miss something at the other end of the street. Afterwards everyone can say what they saw. In the moment nobody gets the full picture.

involuntary-2008.title: Involuntary
involuntary-2008.syn:
Summer is about to arrive in Sweden, and minor indiscretions and transgressions quietly spread. Leffe likes to show off in front of his friends and tell crude jokes, especially after a drink. Meanwhile, a self-righteous primary-school teacher has no sense of boundaries: she insists that her fellow educators need some “guidance” too. There are also two teenage girls who love taking sexy photos and partying. Then, one night in a park, a complete stranger finds one of the girls passed out drunk. With a humorous eye, the film examines the lessons we should learn, the lectures we give, and the lines that must never be crossed.

Two other stories unfold at a party and on a coach. A host hurt by fireworks tries to keep his dinner going. A bus driver stops the journey until someone owns up to damage inside the coach. Across the five stories, people sometimes comply to avoid spoiling the mood, and a person who speaks up can become the source of everyone else’s discomfort.
involuntary-2008.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
involuntary-2008.st:
The director co-wrote the film with Erik Hemmendorff and worked with cinematographer Marius Dybwad Brandrud. In Östlund’s second feature, editing brings similar moments of hesitation, silence and pressure into contact across five independent stories. The Swedish Film Institute selected it as Sweden’s submission for the foreign-language Oscar.

The film consists of five unconnected stories, all about the pressure a group puts on an individual. Carrying over a habit from ski films — where a cut usually signals a failure — Östlund relies on uncut long takes; the longest scene runs seven minutes.

It premiered in Un Certain Regard at the 61st Cannes Film Festival on 19 May 2008 and was Sweden’s submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film the following year.
highlights: Watch when doorframes, seatbacks or the edges of the frame hide someone’s face. With no easy reaction shot, voices and silences have to tell you what happened.
Pair it with Autobiographical Scene Number 6882, where a small promise similarly becomes something a person has to live up to in front of others.

autobiographical-scene-6882.title: Autobiographical Scene Number 6882
autobiographical-scene-6882.syn:
On Sweden’s west coast, a 30-year-old man is celebrating Midsummer’s Eve with his friends. He calls them all over to watch, because he is about to jump into the sea from a very high bridge.

From the campsite the bridge is part of the scenery. Once Martin calls his friends over, the jump becomes something everyone has come to see. The closer he gets to the moment, the more he has to weigh his body’s reluctance against what he promised aloud.
autobiographical-scene-6882.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
autobiographical-scene-6882.st:
Östlund co-wrote the film with Erik Hemmendorff and handled the cinematography and editing. Holding the bridge, spectators and hesitation together echoes his earlier skiing films’ interest in a movement from beginning to end. It also pairs well with Involuntary, another film that locates social pressure in a physical act.

Filmed during Midsummer in Smögen, a small town on Sweden’s west coast, the short continues Östlund’s quasi-documentary method of recording everyday life from a fixed camera, set to music by Schubert.

It won the Special Jury Prize (François Ode Award) at the 2005 Hamburg International Short Film Festival and the Prix UIP at Edinburgh, and was nominated for Best Short at the 2006 Guldbagge Awards.
highlights: Take in how much room the bridge occupies and how small the jumper looks. The wide shot lets height register before we are told how to feel.
Listen to Schubert alongside the voices at the bridge. One sound prepares us for a feat, while the other keeps it an afternoon among friends.

autobiographical-scene-6882.editorial: The nine minutes are built around waiting. Once Martin calls an audience over, backing out becomes a public act too. The film gives him time to hesitate and gives the viewer time to realise that they are also waiting for him to keep his promise.

the-guitar-mongoloid.title: The Guitar Mongoloid
the-guitar-mongoloid.syn:
The film follows a group of people living outside social norms in the fictional city of “Jöteborg”, strikingly similar to the real Gothenburg. Although it is not a documentary, most of the people on screen are non-professional actors more or less playing themselves.

A boy singing homemade punk songs turns up on rooftops and street corners. Elsewhere, grown men play with guns and a woman struggles with fear. Tram lines, the river and housing blocks connect the fragments. The boy’s songs keep bringing the film back outside and form a loose link between people who generally go their own ways.
the-guitar-mongoloid.bio: Ruben Östlund (b. 1974, Sweden) is a director and screenwriter. He studied at the University of Gothenburg, and his early years making ski films shaped his signature long-take style. He examines social order, power relations and the complexities of human nature through cool, darkly humorous absurdist storytelling. In 2010 his short Incident by a Bank won the Golden Bear for Best Short Film at the 60th Berlin International Film Festival. In 2014 Force Majeure won the Un Certain Regard Jury Prize at the 67th Cannes Film Festival. In 2017 The Square, a satire of the contemporary art world and social morality, won the Palme d’Or at the 70th Cannes Film Festival and received Golden Globe and Academy Award nominations. In 2022 Triangle of Sadness turned to class difference and power, winning the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival and three Academy Award nominations.
the-guitar-mongoloid.st:
Östlund began with fragmentary scenes jotted down while studying in France. Back in Sweden, a meeting with street musician Erik Rutström gave him a way to connect them. A later Gothenburg Film Festival screening in association with the Swedish Cinematheque highlighted the city preserved in the film’s early digital images.

Östlund has said the debut began with a young street musician, Erik Rutström, he saw playing on Kungsgatan in Gothenburg: uncensored, relaxed and full of energy. Most of the people on screen are non-professionals playing themselves.

The film opened in Swedish cinemas on 1 October 2004, won the FIPRESCI Prize at the Moscow International Film Festival the following year, and was nominated for the 2005 Nordic Council Film Prize.
highlights: Notice the roofs, river and trams in the early digital imagery. The fictional city retains the textures of the streets where it was filmed.
Treat Erik Rutström’s songs as a thread through the film. Listen to how a sound or lyric carries from one place or group of characters to the next.

the-guitar-mongoloid.editorial: Start with the TV antennas on the roof. Downstairs people are watching the same show, and the boy interferes with a city evening running to schedule. The episodes that follow extend that moment: when someone departs from the accepted way of living, where does the camera settle, and for how long?

faith-lacking-deed-lies-dead.title: Faith Lacking Deed Lies Death
faith-lacking-deed-lies-dead.syn: Albert Serra begins with the textured surfaces and enigmatic markings of Antoni Tàpies’s paintings. Layered images bring figures, light and landscape together in the dark, while fragments of text appear among them. Image and sound guide the viewer through an experiment in faith, matter and perception.
faith-lacking-deed-lies-dead.bio: Albert Serra is a Catalan filmmaker from Banyoles whose work encompasses film and museum installations. His features include Honour of the Knights, The Death of Louis XIV and the Cannes competition film Pacifiction. Afternoons of Solitude won the Golden Shell in San Sebastián.
faith-lacking-deed-lies-dead.st: Commissioned by Barcelona's Museu Tàpies, the film revisits the painter after his centenary. Serra and cinematographer-editor Román Bayarri echo the artist’s material practice through digital superimposition, building shots from multiple layers. Marc Verdaguer composed the music. Hainan uses the English title ending in Death, while international catalogues often use Dead. The museum lists 52 minutes, and FIDMarseille lists 53.
faith-lacking-deed-lies-dead.editorial: Allow the 53 minutes for an experiment in looking. Watch for what happens to a beam of light as it passes through overlapping images and for the moments when a human figure separates from the background.
highlights: Watch how layers alter colour and the outline of a figure.
Follow the rhythms of the text, the score and the still bodies separately.

from-dawn-to-dawn-2026.title: From Dawn to Dawn
from-dawn-to-dawn-2026.syn: A Wen, a 38-year-old businessman in Barcelona, is filmmaker Xisi Sofia Ye Chen’s brother. They grew up watching Hong Kong gangster films on VHS, and A Wen later became involved with local gangs. As Ye Chen returns to his daily life, his work, family obligations and sleepless nights open up a history that was difficult to discuss at home.
from-dawn-to-dawn-2026.bio: Born in Barcelona in 1994 to Chinese parents, Xisi Sofia Ye Chen grew up speaking Qingtianese, Mandarin, Catalan and Spanish. She studied humanities and creative documentary at Pompeu Fabra University. From Dawn to Dawn, her first feature, draws on her interest in migration, family and belonging.
from-dawn-to-dawn-2026.st: The project grew from memories shared by the filmmaker and her brother. Childhood VHS tapes became a way to talk about the past. In the present, conversations around family, depression, insomnia and feng shui make space for the details of daily life. Pablo Paloma shot the film and Juliana Montañés edited it. Visions du Réel lists 93 minutes and DokuFest lists 96.
from-dawn-to-dawn-2026.editorial: Consider the gangster films the siblings grew up with alongside the documentary’s patient attention to what adulthood demands of A Wen. The filmmaker’s unusual access as his sister also allows the silences between them to carry weight.
highlights: Watch how the brotherhood of the old films compares with the duties A Wen has in the present.
Listen to when people switch languages, and whom they address in each.

let-us-through-dear-ancestors.title: Let Us through, Dear Ancestors
let-us-through-dear-ancestors.syn: In 1617 a Spanish friar, Father Enciso, rules an island in the Philippines. In the name of salvation he takes control of land, labour and bodies. The islanders first receive the visitors according to their own customs, then find ways to resist or survive as their space for living contracts.
let-us-through-dear-ancestors.bio: Filipino filmmaker Lav Diaz works as a director, writer and cinematographer. From What Is Before won Locarno’s Golden Leopard, and The Woman Who Left won the Golden Lion in Venice. Magellan and his other films look at the long effects of colonialism and dictatorship, often through black-and-white images and extended takes.
let-us-through-dear-ancestors.st: Following Magellan’s depiction of early contact, Diaz moves to the seventeenth century, when imperial rule has entered everyday life. His Venice director’s statement connects evangelisation to the forced labour behind churches, ports and forts. Diaz wrote, photographed and edited the film.
let-us-through-dear-ancestors.editorial: Set aside an alert stretch of the day for this one. In the time Diaz leaves the camera in place, the arrangement of bodies in a room starts to tell its own story about power. It makes a rewarding companion to Magellan.
highlights: Watch the gestures and forms of address the islanders use to maintain their own ways of living.
Notice how doors, windows and walls divide the same space between people.

lover-not-a-fighter-2026.title: Lover, Not a Fighter
lover-not-a-fighter-2026.syn: Andrej makes rules for a quieter summer: help his grandmother, avoid most people and stop getting so drunk that he climbs trees he cannot get down from. Then he shares a Fanta with Miša. As they grow closer, their friends, families and hesitant ideas about intimacy get in the way.
lover-not-a-fighter-2026.bio: Slovak writer-director Martina Buchelová made the shorts Magic Moments, R+J and Who Wants to Be a Hero? and co-directed the documentary Kam patrím? Lover, Not a Fighter is her solo narrative feature debut and won the Proxima Grand Prix in Karlovy Vary.
lover-not-a-fighter-2026.st: This Slovak-Czech co-production was written and directed by Buchelová and shot by Adam Mach. Ninja Film and NOCHI FILM were among the producers. Set over a summer, the story gives its characters time to play, talk and make mistakes. It premiered in Karlovy Vary’s Proxima Competition.
lover-not-a-fighter-2026.editorial: An easy pick for a lighter slot in this lineup. Notice what happens before anyone works up the nerve to speak. A shared soft drink or a brief hesitation often says more about what it is to be that age than a declaration can.
highlights: Start with Andrej’s rules and watch which ones are the first to go.
Notice how the awkwardness changes when the pair are alone or among friends.

the-daughters-of-abraham.title: The Daughters of Abraham
the-daughters-of-abraham.syn: Myriam, from a Muslim family in Marseille, reconnects with Eva, who comes from a Jewish family, after years apart. During a summer together they find pockets of freedom away from home. When a crisis pulls in their friends and relatives, they must decide what they can do for each other and what the friendship may cost them.
the-daughters-of-abraham.bio: Hanaël El Yousfi grew up in Provence in a family of Moroccan heritage. She studied law before moving into filmmaking. The Daughters of Abraham, her feature debut, draws on a setting she knows and follows the pressure that family and public life can put on a friendship.
the-daughters-of-abraham.st: El Yousfi collaborated with Raphaël Chevènement and Mia Grace Brown on the screenplay. Produced by CG Cinéma and France 2 Cinéma, the film places the two friends in the everyday social life of Marseille. It won the Audience Award and a Special Mention in Angoulême and screened in TIFF’s Discovery section.
the-daughters-of-abraham.editorial: Start by watching how easy the friends are with each other after years apart. Later, when people tell them where their loyalties should lie, those early scenes give you a way to weigh what is being asked of them.
highlights: Listen to what can be said at home, in front of friends, and in private.
Notice how the streets and social spaces the pair can move through change after the crisis.

the-spiral-2026.title: The Spiral
the-spiral-2026.syn: On a stormy night Anna arrives at her daughter Alice’s flat in Rome. Twenty years earlier, Alice nearly lost a leg in an accident. Anna says a stranger saved it in exchange for a deal. As Anna begins to tell her what happened, Alice must find out who paid the price and whether she can make a decision of her own.
the-spiral-2026.bio: Paolo Strippoli is an Italian screenwriter and director whose films include the co-directed A Classic Horror Story and his work on Flowing and The Holy Boy. He brings horror into intimate settings. The Spiral was selected for competition at Venice.
the-spiral-2026.st: Strippoli and Salvatore de Chirico had been developing the story for years. Speaking in Venice, Strippoli described how horror gave him room to explore control within a family. Propaganda Italia worked with Italian, French and Belgian partners on the film. Valeria Bruni Tedeschi plays the stranger.
the-spiral-2026.editorial: Watch the reasons Anna gives for her choice and the moment Alice begins asking her own questions. The conflict is especially sharp when both women remember the same act of protection differently.
highlights: Notice who controls the story before and after the storm.
Watch how later information changes the meaning of the family portrait.

time-and-water-2026.title: Time and Water
time-and-water-2026.syn: As Iceland’s glaciers recede and his grandparents die, writer Andri Snær Magnason gathers family films and photographs. Working with Sara Dosa, he combines them with glacier archives, songs and folktales in a time capsule for future viewers. The film asks what can be passed on when familiar places and the people who remember them are disappearing.
time-and-water-2026.bio: Sara Dosa is an American documentary director and producer whose films include The Last Season, The Seer and the Unseen and Fire of Love. The latter was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Documentary Feature. She often works with archives left by participants to explore how people inhabit landscapes.
time-and-water-2026.st: Inspired by Magnason’s nonfiction book On Time and Water, the film combines family albums with scientific footage, folk songs and oral histories. National Geographic Documentary Films took part in the production and release. Festival listings put the running time at around 90 to 93 minutes.
time-and-water-2026.editorial: A good choice for viewers drawn to the archive material in Fire of Love and the stories people tell about their families. When an old picture of a glacier meets a family photograph, consider who remembers what they show and who will come to know them through the images alone.
highlights: Notice how photographs, home movies and scientific footage record time differently.
Listen for what the songs and stories carry that measurements cannot.

woman-unknown-2026.title: Woman Unknown
woman-unknown-2026.syn: After the German occupation of Denmark ends, a young maid named Marie is about to marry her employer, the wealthy widower Christian. She had a relationship with a German soldier during the war. As people begin to investigate what their neighbours did under occupation, Marie tries to hold on to the place she has earned and decide how long she can conceal her past.
woman-unknown-2026.bio: May el-Toukhy is a Danish filmmaker of Danish and Egyptian heritage. She directed Long Story Short and Queen of Hearts and has directed for The Crown. Queen of Hearts won the Sundance World Cinema Dramatic Audience Award. Woman Unknown, her third feature, reunites her with writer Maren Louise Käehne.
woman-unknown-2026.st: The project grew from research into women publicly humiliated and attacked after the Danish liberation because of their relationships with German soldiers. The filmmakers heard few first-person testimonies. They placed this history within five days of Marie’s life, played by Mathilde Arcel.
woman-unknown-2026.editorial: Follow where Marie walks through the house and who has the right to sit where. The quiet division between a maid’s spaces and her prospective place as mistress of the house makes the stakes of the returning gossip tangible.
highlights: Watch how access to the same house changes with Marie’s position in it.
Compare what other people say about Marie during the war with the choices you see her make over the film’s five days.

another-green-world-2026.title: Another Green World
another-green-world-2026.syn: A graduate returns to a small southern city to look for work and befriends a driving pupil. His sister, a tour guide, prepares for a contest. The local legend of Mount Lanke takes on a different shape in each of their lives.
another-green-world-2026.bio: Wang Kejing comes from Quzhou, where the Lanke legend is rooted. She wrote and directed this debut feature. She studied photography and related media at Massachusetts College of Art and Design. Her documentary short Kayaking premiered at Doclisboa.
another-green-world-2026.st: Developed through the Beijing market and a Macau work-in-progress programme, the film was shot by Shi Shuo. Wang also served as one of four editors. The legend of a man who returns from a brief mountain visit to find that generations have passed sits alongside the repeated routines of driving lessons and tour guiding.
another-green-world-2026.editorial: Track the driving routes and the guided tours. Both depend on repetition, and both let the film show what changes when someone leaves the prescribed route.
highlights: The Lanke legend changes with each telling.

cassowary-2026.title: Cassowary
cassowary-2026.syn: Sumin works at an airport keeping birds away. After a typhoon and a fire, she returns to her island family. An elusive cassowary unsettles what three generations of women have learned to live with.
cassowary-2026.bio: Zhang Hanyi made his feature debut with Life After Life, rooted in China's Loess Plateau. His follow-up, supported by Jia Zhangke's Young Director Support Program, concentrates on four members of a family living on an island.
cassowary-2026.st: Shanghai's programme identifies Sumin's airport job and the fire at home. Her job is to keep birds away; on the island she is drawn to one. In a festival interview, Zhang described a desire to move from a recognisable, strongly local landscape to a more abstract space for the family.
cassowary-2026.editorial: Pay attention to pauses and to who feels free to speak. The cassowary can be read through the different reactions it draws from people who share a house and very different memories.
highlights: Sumin's work and her search for the bird mirror one another.

four-seasons-in-java-2026.syn: After twenty years in prison, Pertiwi returns to her Javanese village, finds unlikely allies and confronts the four men whose actions led to her imprisonment.
four-seasons-in-java-2026.bio: Indonesian writer-director Kamila Andini made The Seen and Unseen, Yuni and Before, Now & Then. Yuni won TIFF's Platform Prize.

four-seasons-in-java-2026.editorial: A revenge story offers four obvious targets. The deeper question is what the rest of the village did, and how beautiful, open landscapes can still hem someone in.
highlights: Look for how the seasons organise Pertiwi's return.
Notice the tension between the landscape and the village's social order.

head-to-head-2026.bio: The Tehran-born director made shorts including Online Shopping, Limbo and Horn. This is her debut feature.

master-rezwan-shahriar-sumit-2026.title: Master
master-rezwan-shahriar-sumit-2026.syn: Jahir, a respected teacher, wins a local election in Mohanganj. At first backed by young people with high hopes, he gradually compromises his principles and alienates his wife and closest ally.
master-rezwan-shahriar-sumit-2026.bio: Bangladeshi filmmaker Rezwan Shahriar Sumit's first feature, The Salt in Our Waters, follows a coastal fishing community. His second turns that interest in how communities organise themselves towards local politics.
master-rezwan-shahriar-sumit-2026.st: IFFR places the drama against the local power structures that preceded Bangladesh's political upheaval in 2024. Rallies, favours and conversations at home give Jahir repeated opportunities to rationalise small compromises.
master-rezwan-shahriar-sumit-2026.editorial: Look for the first favour Jahir grants and the cost of taking it back. The thriller gathers force in these small decisions and in how his wife and allies begin to speak to him.

the-remotes-2026.title: The Remotes
the-remotes-2026.syn: Days before emigrating, a grieving detective pursues a link between a navigation app and his wife's fatal crash. A recording of his sister-in-law's voice might explain how the app changes its users' behaviour.
the-remotes-2026.bio: Manila-based filmmaker, musician and artist John Torres made Todo Todo Teros, Lukas the Strange and People Power Bombshell. His work brings personal recordings, documentary observation and fiction together.
the-remotes-2026.st:
The New York Film Festival identifies the political surveillance following the Duterte-era drug war as one context for the film. Diversion acquired world sales ahead of Toronto. A navigation voice, recorded speech and telepathy make listening part of the investigation.

New York lists 150 minutes. The sales materials list 153 minutes, a 1.66:1 aspect ratio and 5.1 sound. The Hainan screening runtime awaits confirmation.
the-remotes-2026.editorial: Notice when you begin to trust the navigation voice and when that trust slips. Torres scatters procedural clues across ordinary commutes, voice recordings and grief.
highlights: Listen for directions, recordings and who gets to issue commands.

water-of-the-sea-2026.syn: An estranged brother asks Chen Weidong to take their ageing mother back to their father's southern hometown. A flight together brings the family into contact with memories they have spent decades keeping apart.
water-of-the-sea-2026.bio: Zhou Lidong wrote and directed Autumn Fields and returned with a new feature eight years later. His work attends to ordinary livelihoods and the ways kinship bears the weight of history.
